PTI Chairman Gohar moves PHC against emergency, governor's rule in KP
items.description: PESHAWAR: PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Wednesday moved the Peshawar High Court (PHC) against the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, requesting the court to declare the move unconstitutional. Advocate Shah Faisal Ilyas submitted the petition on behalf of the PTI chairman. The petitioner requested the PHC to declare the Oct 11 emergency proclamation as “unconstitutional, ultra vires, coram non judice, tainted with malice in law and fact, devoid of objective material, and of no legal effect”; and urged it to set the proclamation aside. Barrister Gohar is represented by a panel of lawyers, including Barrister Sameer Khosa, Salman Akram Raja, Ali Zaman, Sardar Haseeb Ahmad and Zainab Shahid. Filed under Article 199 (Jurisdiction of High Court) of the Constitution of Pakistan, the petition named the Federation of Pakistan (through the secretaries of the Cabinet, law ministry, interior ministry and defence ministry); the province of KP; KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi; the speaker of the KP Assembly, and the secretary of the KP Home and Tribal Affairs Department as respondents. More to follow

items.title: Éducation à Kankan : un déficit de 736 enseignants, la DPE lance un cri d’alarme
items.description: À Kankan, le manque d’enseignants perturbe le fonctionnement de plusieurs établissements scolaires, particulièrement dans l’enseignement élémentaire. Face à cette situation, le directeur préfectoral de l’Éducation, Souleymane Daffé, appelle les autorités à agir rapidement pour combler le déficit, alors que l’année scolaire 2026 a démarré le 5 octobre sur l’ensemble du territoire national. Selon les données communiquées par le directeur préfectoral de l’Éducation (DPE), les besoins en personnel enseignant dans la préfecture sont estimés à 736 enseignants, dont 630 pour l’élémentaire et 106 pour le secondaire . Cette insuffisance s’explique notamment par l’augmentation des effectifs scolaires, les départs à la retraite et les décès d’enseignants. Une situation que les recrutements effectués jusque-là ne permettent pas de compenser, selon Souleymane Daffé. « Après l’engagement de 2024, il n’y a pas eu d’autre recrutement. Chaque année, des enseignants partent à la retraite, tandis que le nombre d’élèves scolarisés augmente. S’il n’y a pas de recrutement pour remplacer ceux qui partent, le besoin en enseignants se fait forcément sentir », explique-t-il. D’après les statistiques présentées par le responsable préfectoral, les établissements scolaires relevant de la DPE de Kankan, y compris ceux des localités récemment rattachées à son ressort, notamment Tokounou et Sabadou-Baranama, comptent actuellement 2 223 enseignants en activité . Cet effectif se répartit entre 1 361 enseignants dans l’enseignement élémentaire et 862 dans le secondaire. Malgré ces ressources humaines, le déficit reste important et affecte particulièrement les écoles primaires. Dans certaines localités rurales, la situation est préoccupante : des établissements disposant de quatre classes ne comptent parfois qu’un ou deux enseignants pour assurer les cours. « Tous les enseignants ne sont pas au complet, surtout à l’élémentaire. Il y a des villages où, pour quatre classes, on ne dispose souvent que d’un ou deux enseignants », déplore Souleymane Daffé. Des solutions locales pour maintenir les cours Face à cette pénurie, les responsables éducatifs tentent de limiter les conséquences sur les apprentissages. La DPE privilégie notamment une gestion locale des difficultés, sans procéder à des permutations d’enseignants qui pourraient, selon son directeur, aggraver le déficit dans certaines écoles. Dans plusieurs localités, les Associations des parents et amis de l’école (APAE) apportent également leur contribution au maintien des activités pédagogiques. Elles prennent notamment en charge des enseignants contractuels pour renforcer les équipes en poste. Souleymane Daffé salue cette mobilisation communautaire, qui permet de soutenir les établissements confrontés au manque de personnel. Il souligne toutefois que cet appui ne saurait constituer une réponse durable aux besoins de la préfecture. L’espoir placé dans le recrutement de 6 000 enseignants Pour réduire le déficit, la DPE mise désormais sur le recrutement annoncé de 6 000 enseignants au niveau national dans la fonction publique. Selon Souleymane Daffé, cette opération pourrait contribuer à améliorer la situation à Kankan, même si elle ne permettra pas nécessairement de combler tous les besoins. Le directeur préfectoral appelle ainsi les autorités compétentes à accélérer le processus de recrutement et d’affectation afin que les établissements les plus touchés puissent bénéficier rapidement de nouveaux enseignants. « Nous avons un grand espoir avec le recrutement annoncé. Cela ne corrigera pas définitivement le déficit, mais permettra de réduire les besoins. Nous demandons à l’État d’accélérer les choses, car l’année scolaire a déjà commencé. Un retard supplémentaire d’un à deux mois dans la mise à disposition des enseignants risque d’entraîner des retards dans les programmes scolaires », prévient-il. Alors que les cours ont repris depuis le 5 octobre 2027, le renforcement du personnel enseignant demeure un défi majeur pour la DPE de Kankan. La rapidité des recrutements et des affectations sera déterminante pour améliorer les conditions d’apprentissage, notamment dans les zones rurales où le manque d’enseignants compromet déjà le bon déroulement des cours.

items.title: National Assembly passes resolution endorsing Centre's imposition of emergency in KP
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The National Assembly on Wednesday passed a resolution endorsing the federal government’s imposition of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The Centre had imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP on Sunday, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The NA question hour session was suspended due to discussions on the emergency. Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry tabled a motion regarding the proclamation of emergency, which was adopted with a majority vote after a discussion opened by Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar. “The National Assembly approves the Proclamation of Emergency issued by the President on the 11th October, 2026 in the Province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under second proviso of clause (1) of Article 232 of the Constitution,” read a post by NA’s official X account. According to Article 232 , if the “president acts on his own, the proclamation of emergency shall be placed” before both Houses of the Parliament for approval by each House within 10 days. The proclamation of emergency is now pending approval by the Senate. Meanwhile, a proclamation for governor’s rule issued under Article 234 “shall be laid before a joint sitting and shall cease to be in force at the expiration of two months”, unless a joint sitting approves its extension. However, such a measure shall not remain in force for more than six months. Throughout Wednesday’s proceedings, opposition members participated calmly and did not stage any loud protest, unlike past instances of ruckus when PTI objects to the Centre. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also attended part of the session, with pictures released by the NA showing him shaking hands with Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai. Federal ministers defended the emergency imposition while assailing what they described as the PTI-led KP government’s lack of will to combat terrorism. In tune with that, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari blamed the PTI for the circumstances that compelled the Centre to impose emergency in KP and termed it a “political suicide attack” for the party. However, he also urged the treasury and the opposition to get back on the path of dialogue and make joint efforts against terrorism. At one point during the proceedings, NA Speaker Ayaz Sadiq noted that the Oct 3 dialogue was held in a cordial atmosphere. Sadiq praised both sides for “attempting more than their capacity so that the matter is settled”. However, he said some matters were beyond the parties’ control and voiced his support for forming the same committees for negotiations if ever needed in the future. Addressing PTI lawmakers, the speaker said, “Everyone’s response was that this [process of dialogue] should continue, but you also understand that your hands were tied.” He took note of the PTI’s complaints regarding the jail conditions of party founder Imran Khan, adding that he had even provided details of facilities provided to the jailed ex-premier. The session was adjourned to meet again at 11am on Oct 16 (Friday). ‘Political suicide attack’ Bilawal began his speech by highlighting that emergency and governor’s rule in KP were measures taken under the Constitution . Reading the relevant provisions, he asserted that the Centre tried its best to “engage the opposition so this step did not have to be taken”. “They will have to accept, even if not publicly, but the responsible leadership of the opposition knows that the PTI itself carried out a political suicide attack on its KP government,” he remarked. The PPP chief maintained that the PTI could not deny that its “leadership, particularly in the province had a key role in the political, constitutional and legal circumstances” at present. Bilawal emphasised that the PPP’s stance was that “before employing this constitutional atomic bomb, we must engage with PTI and the opposition and try to address the federal government’s reservations that they were not supporting them in the war against terrorism”. He observed: “If political space is restricted for one political party, it is impossible that it remains restricted for that particular party; it is limited for every political party, political worker and Pakistani citizen. “We are responsible for this, but you cannot deny that you are also responsible for it,” he said. Terming the imposition of emergency a “difficult decision”, Bilawal recalled alleged remarks by Sohail Afridi — the KP chief minister whose role is now non-functional — that he would not combat terrorism the way the Centre wanted. “If this was not a political suicide, then what else was it?” The Bhutto scion wondered if the opposition and Afridi had left any reason for President Asif Ali Zardari, who he said prides himself on passing the 18th Amendment, to “refuse to sign” the emergency proclamation. He argued that due to the PTI’s actions and statements, neither the president, the Centre, nor he had any legal or political reason left for not imposing emergency in KP. “But even today, I would recommend to the federal government that we extend our hand forward once again for negotiations, political discussions and try to find a resolution and a middle path,” Bilawal added. The PPP chairman noted that emergency was “always a stopgap measure”. “We cannot sustain the emergency forever,” he added, emphasising that while the counterterrorism fight would be better than before, an “all-of-society and all-of-country response” was needed to eradicate it completely. Regarding the Oct 3 talks of a joint delegation of the PPP and the government with the opposition, Bilawal said, “Late at night, I was informed that congratulations, negotiations are succeeding.” He said the PTI was willing to declare the areas in KP with surging terrorism as “terrorist areas”, and the opposition was about to agree that the federal and KP governments would sign a pact on joint efforts against terrorism. However, the dialogue collapsed. The former foreign minister pointed out that the security challenges Pakistan was facing were “way more complicated” than before, adding that India “could still not digest […] its embarrassment” from the May 2025 conflict . Referring to remarks by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi that its ‘ Operation Sindoor ’ was still ongoing, Bilawal said: “It means that India is still sponsoring terrorist incidents in Pakistan, sometimes in the form of TTP (Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan) and sometimes in the form of separatist terrorist groups.” He reiterated Pakistan’s stance that India was involved in terrorist activities being conducted from across the Afghan border. The ex-foreign minister then highlighted Islamabad’s role as a mediator in the US-Iran war. “But there is a state — which we do not recognise as a state — that will neither be happy nor ever forget that you took this step. And those Zionist forces will and are interfering in Pakistan’s internal politics and state.” Concluding his speech, the PPP chairman emphasised the need for building consensus on “some fundamental issues” for an empowered lower house. “Even today, we are saying, come and at least begin from this house,” he said while addressing the opposition benches. Gohar demands implementation of NAP Speaking on the NA floor, PTI Chairman Gohar Ali Khan’s said his party “rejected” the Centre’s move to impose emergency in KP. He asked what “terrorism” Imran’s wife or sisters had allegedly been involved in that they had been put behind bars, or what the accusations were against the PTI MNAs and MPAs who he said were detained. Gohar further said, “One person is not present in the house currently. When he comes during a joint session, then I will reveal the reality of the negotiations.” He affirmed that the PTI had raised its voice against terrorism, adding that measures against the scourge must be taken according to the National Action Plan (NAP). Gohar argued that the PML-N opposition during the PTI’s tenure carried out “14 long marches in two years, but you did not let us stage even one long march”. Presenting his version of the Oct 3 talks with the government, the PTI leader said his party was being asked to immediately call off the long march . “I said where did [the topic] of terrorism arise from suddenly.” Noting that the government had put forward “five reservations”, Gohar said PTI was willing to make the KP Police Act similar to that of Punjab and Sindh. The PTI leader reiterated his party’s request for the production of certain MNAs it says were taken into custody. Gohar also welcomed Bilawal’s proposal to continue dialogue. Responding to Gohar’s remarks, the PPP chairman said the PTI was busy in its long march while the people of KP were being targeted by terrorists. Bilawal reiterated that the opposition could keep arguing against the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, but no one could deny that the decision was grounded in the Constitution. “I cannot insist on the government to continue talks with PTI despite being defrauded multiple times,” the PPP chairman said. Pointing towards Gohar and Achakzai, Bilawal said: “I believe that none of them is allied with terrorists. I believe that they will definitely want to combat terrorism; however, they cannot deny the fact that their former chief minister contradicted this fact.” Bilawal again requested all the stakeholders to unite and combat terrorism collectively. He also called for the provision of all facilities to the incarcerated PTI founder. ‘Threat to national security’ Addressing the house, the law minister explained that emergency was imposed in KP as the security situation there was becoming a threat to “national security”. Tarar noted that after the proclamation of emergency was issued, the Constitution’s Article 232 required that both houses of the parliament approve the measure. He recalled that the federal cabinet examined “material” regarding terrorism in the province during its Oct 11 meeting and then advised PM Shehbaz to recommend the imposition of emergency. He noted that some people compared the measure to the emergency imposed by former dictator Gen Pervez Musharraf on Oct 12, 1999. The minister particularly noted “internal disturbances” and cross-border infiltrations. He contended that the situation since Oct 15, 2025, when Sohail Afridi’s government came into power in KP , was “turning into a threat to national security to an alarming extent”. He went on to highlight that there was a rise in terrorism in KP, especially after 2021, due to the approach of the provincial government. “Perhaps there might be foreign, diplomatic and political reasons behind it, which got inflamed due to a political party’s point of view.” Tarar stated that 2,911 incidents of terrorism took place between 2021 and 2024 in KP, but they surged to 3,787 incidents between Oct 15, 2025 and Oct 9, 2026. He criticised the KP chief minister for ignoring martyred security and police personnel, and for instead preferring to promote his political designs and make visits across the country. “Even this was announced that the federal capital will be conquered,” he said, referring to the party’s plan to hold a protest long march towards the federal capital. The PML-N leader expressed his government’s gratitude to NA Speaker Ayaz Sadiq for providing a platform for dialogue between the Centre and the opposition. He reiterated the government’s stance that the PTI had the agreement draft changed multiple times, but even then backed off from it. Tarar observed that the PTI demanded the release of their party founder Imran Khan and his treatment in a private hospital despite knowing that only courts could provide such a relief. He said two days would be “remembered in the country’s democratic history with regard to misfortune and a political party”. On the emergency measure, the law minister noted that a special mechanism has been introduced for 12 districts of KP. Speaking after Tarar, Achakzai criticised him for trying to prove that terrorism was not tackled in KP. The opposition leader questioned the government’s mandate in the February 2024 general elections, quipping that the opposition would “surrender” if the minister could swear that the government won those polls fairly. Achakzai alleged that the incumbent ruling coalition was formed “illegally”. ‘You do not have clean hands’ Meanwhile, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif went on to recall the tenure of the PTI government in the Centre and assailed the party’s past actions. Referring to ex-prime minister Imran Khan’s plan to resettle members of the TTP, he said PTI tried to convince the then-opposition that “bringing these terrorists back would be better for Pakistan”. The PML-N leader mentioned the 2019 episode of an Indian pilot’s capture in Pakistan: “They had threatened and we were surrendering. The then-prime minister was saying, ‘What should I do? Attack India?’” Asif urged the opposition to reflect on its past actions, adding that Imran often used to praise former army chief retired General Qamar Javed Bajwa. “As long as this contradiction remains in our words and actions and in our society, the circumstances of this country will not fix.” He narrated his time behind bars during the PTI government, when Shehbaz “smuggled a blanket” to him to brace the low temperatures. “I used to eat the jail’s food,” he said, claiming that orders were given to remove the geyser when it was installed. “But we did not hold rallies or mourn at D-Chowk or dig graves. We did not martyr police and law enforcement personnel,” Asif remarked. “You demand equity when you have clean hands. You do not have clean hands, you cannot demand equity; this is a thousand-year-old principle,” he contended. “You know very well what Gen Musharraf did to me. There was a 4x6 cell in Attock jail,” the PML-N politician said, emphasising that he stood with his party and ex-PM Nawaz Sharif. Speaking on the current political situation, Asif alleged that Afridi used to “take directives […] from a person sitting in Afghanistan”. He referred to a statement by the TTP condemning the imposition of emergency and deployment of troops in certain places. “Who is their ally and who is their rival?” he said. The minister further countered the PTI’s stance that its leaders have not been able to meet Imran, who is imprisoned in the Adiala jail. “Meetings are held, [but] a lot of them are not publicised or brought on record,” he maintained. Farooq Sattar urges PTI to ‘openly condemn terrorism’ In his remarks on the floor of the lower house, Farooq Sattar expressed Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan’s (MQM-P) confidence in the decision taken by the prime minister. “This was an extremely difficult decision, but so unavoidable that you had no other option,” Sattar said about imposing emergency and governor’s rule. “We trust your decision as we trust your experience, capabilities, political acumen, and that you made this decision in the interest of the nation,” he added. The MQM-P lawmaker contended that the PTI was “on the wrong side and does not have concrete arguments” to declare that the decision was baseless or made with political motives. “The main issue is of the mindset,” he declared, adding that Imran had “publicly said that the war on terror is not ours”. “This is their policy. This is their mindset.” Sattar questioned whether the KP government had ever published reports to expose terrorist hideouts and extremist trends. He further raised questions about the government’s pursuit of cases against suspected terrorists. “Openly condemn terrorism; else, the allegation of backing [it], if a commission is formed and God forbid, it is proven in the inquiry that there is political extremism and terrorism complicity, there is a nexus, then where will you go?” Sattar recounted his past MQM experiences, saying, “I have also suffered such times. A lot of times, the narrative coming from the top was difficult to defend. Today, I feel that Barrister Gohar is also not in the position to defend his [party’s] position on KP.”

items.title: Tunisian journalists fear jail again as freedoms erode
items.description: By Tarek Amara TUNIS, Oct 14 (Reuters) - Journalists in Tunisia who enjoyed a burst of press freedom after the 2011 Arab Spring are once again looking over their shoulders in the knowledge their work may land them in prison. The 2011 overthrow of autocrat Zine El-Abidine Ben Ali unshackled Tunisia's media, but a decade later President Kais Saied's seizure of sweeping powers began eroding those gains.

items.title: Regulator expects Man City appeal to be heard by January
items.description: The chair of English football’s Independent Regulator has said he expects Manchester City’s appeal after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules to be heard by January. City, who have repeatedly maintained they are innocent of the charges, are currently top of the Premier League table with six wins out of six following their 3-0 defeat of Liverpool last weekend. No sanction has yet been announced, but City could face a heavy points deduction leading to relegation and there is even been speculation they could be stripped of the three Premier League titles they won between 2009 and 2018. “The Premier League have said that they want to get this resolved within season, and actually, of course, it’s not the Premier League, it’s an independent commission that’s actually going to hear this, made of three retired either judges or lawyers,” Independent Football Regulator (IFR) chair David Kogan told Times Radio on Wednesday. “My understanding is that there is a prescribed process, which is 12 weeks, and so people are assuming this will actually be heard by the middle or the end of January. “But as I say, it’s not our process, it’s that of the Premier League’s independent commission. What I don’t think we can do is take any judgment until we’re quite clear.” Kogan said Tuesday he would resign if there was political interference in any future IFR investigations of City. – Burnham ‘concern’ – British Prime Minister Andy Burnham was criticised for his comments saying he would be “really concerned” if City’s Abu Dhabi owners left the club following the verdict. Downing Street subsequently had to backtrack, insisting no one was “above the rules”. Burnham, who was mayor of Greater Manchester from 2017 to June 2026, has since published all of his dealings with the City hierarchy. On Monday, the Greater Manchester Combined Authority said Burnham had met Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak at an investment summit several years ago when he was mayor of the city. It was also revealed Burnham had spoken to him in the stands at former City captain Vincent Kompany’s testimonial and was accompanied by staff from the club on official overseas visits. Burnham was pressed on the issue during Prime Minister’s Questions in the House of Commons on Wednesday. Jerome Mayhew, an MP for the main opposition Conservative party, asked Burnham if anyone associated with the running of Manchester City had raised the issue of the charges either with him or any member of his team. Burnham replied: “They did not raise those issues with me.” Kogan said earlier Wednesday: “We’ve had absolutely no interference from anybody since we created the regulator a year ago. “We cannot, when regulating football, be subject to political interference on decisions we make about owners, directors or anything else.” He added: “And I won’t actually be prepared to run an organisation which is subject to that degree of interference.” Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca said last week he “completely trusts” the club and believes it will win its appeal. items.title: George Dadzie Junior highly tipped in NDC regional secretary race due to grassroots experience
items.description: George Dadzie Junior, a former Western Regional Youth Organiser of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), is seeking to become the party’s next Western Regional Secretary, with supporters pointing to his experience in party organisation, grassroots mobilisation and member engagement as key strengths. As the party prepares for its regional elections next month, his backers believe his previous leadership role has given him an understanding of the NDC’s organisational structures and the challenges facing the party in the region. Yaw Asomaning, an NDC activist, said hard work was one of the qualities associated with Dadzie Junior’s political career. According to him, Dadzie Junior is regarded by many supporters as a committed party activist who understands the importance of grassroots mobilisation and sustained engagement with members. His supporters believe these qualities would be useful in the Regional Secretary role, which involves coordinating party activities and maintaining communication between regional leadership and the party’s structures. Experience in party organisation Dadzie Junior’s tenure as Western Regional Youth Organiser is another aspect of his candidature highlighted by supporters. They argue that the experience exposed him to grassroots organisation, mobilisation and the coordination required to sustain party activities. Ali Mahad, a long-standing party member, also pointed to his previous experience as relevant to his bid for the position. His backers further cite his interpersonal skills and ability to engage people from different backgrounds, arguing that these could help him work with regional executives, constituency officers and branch members. Samad Sulemana said the Regional Secretary’s role required administrative competence, coordination and the ability to work effectively with other party executives. Supporters believe Dadzie Junior’s relationship-building skills could help promote cooperation within the regional administration. Focus on unity and members’ welfare Party unity and the welfare of grassroots members also feature in the case being made for Dadzie Junior. His supporters say he recognises the need for party members to feel included in decision-making and for their concerns to be addressed beyond election periods. They also cite his willingness to support colleagues and his tolerance of differing views as qualities that could help manage disagreements within the party. In a contest involving aspirants with different support bases, they argue, the ability to listen to opposing views and encourage dialogue would be important in maintaining cohesion. His backers also point to his character and discipline, saying the Regional Secretary must be able to defend the party’s interests while respecting its constitution and established procedures. Delegates to decide The NDC’s Western Regional Secretary contest will test the appeal of the aspirants and their ability to convince delegates of their suitability for the position. For Dadzie Junior’s supporters, his previous leadership experience, knowledge of grassroots politics and emphasis on cooperation make him a credible contender. Ultimately, however, the outcome will depend on the choices of delegates as the party selects its next regional leadership.

items.title: 2027: Police’ll make Nigerians proud in elections – IGP assure
items.description: By Davies Iheamnachor PORT HARCOURT: The Inspector General of Police, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, has assured Nigerians that police would ensure professionalism during the forthcoming general election. Disu stated that the conduct of police personnel before, during and after the election would make Nigerians happy and proud of the force. Disu spoke in Port Harcourt on Tuesday while fielding questions from newsmen after the Launch of a book, “The Origin of Women in Nigeria Police Force”, written by 96-year-old Dame Stella Okuyiga, DCP (rtd), one of the 20 pioneer female Officers of NPF. Disu, who was responding to the questions on the police stance on the 2027 election, said the Force had, in preparation, organised a meeting with Commissioners of police across the country to ensure professionalism during the polls. He said: “I want to let you know that we just finished a conference of all commissioners of police and other senior officers. “We have had two or three elections recently, and you can see that the police came very well and we did so well. We now brought all these experiences together, where we did well and where we did not do well, so that we can perform better in this big election that everybody is looking up to. “I give you my word. Nigeria Police will do so well, and we will make Nigeria Police so proud, and we will make Nigerians proud. On Okuyiga’s book, Disu noted that the author was among the first set of women to join the Nigerian police in 1955, adding that the force is pleased with her recorded achievements. He said: “Mama is 96 years old and she has taken her time to put all her experience, institutional knowledge that she has down in the book for us to be able to study it for generation coming for women police in the next generation coming to have something to look up to. “We in the police, we are starting up the history of not leaving our own, not forgetting our own. “We are going to ensure that we get copies of this book for all police training institutions, for all police officers to go through to see what it was like to be police officers.” However, the author, Okuyiga, DCP (rtd), expressed happiness that the publication was not just a book, but a part of her that would live on. She said: “This book launch today is an important day in my life because the book itself is there. But I still live on my life. I still live on because this book will be in libraries all over the world and they’ll be reading it. “So I’m so happy that with all that is happening today, I will continue to live forever.” The post 2027: Police’ll make Nigerians proud in elections – IGP assure appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Passenger arrivals at airport improved by 23% in first 7 months of 2026
items.description: Passenger arrivals at the international airport and the land borders improved by 23.1% in year-on-year terms to 137,467 in July 2026, the September 2026 Monetary Policy of Report has revealed. This is up from 111,631 arrivals recorded a year ago. Similarly, compared to June 2026, passenger arrivals went up by 15.3%. Cumulatively, for the first seven months of 2026, passenger arrivals increased to 772,250 from 722,020 for the corresponding period in 2025. Ports and Harbours Activity Also, international trade at the country’s two main harbours (Tema and Takoradi), as measured by laden container traffic for inbound and outbound containers, improved during the period under review. Total container traffic increased by 29.0%, year-on-year, to 96,966 in July 2026, up from 75,183 for the corresponding period in 2025. In cumulative terms, total container traffic for the first seven months of 2026 went up by 15.0% to 571,898, compared with 497,292 for the corresponding period of last year.

items.title: AI could cause 'major' incidents within 2 years without safeguards, says Google DeepMind chair
items.description: Artificial intelligence systems could cause “major” security incidents within two years without adequate steps to make them safe as capabilities grow, Google’s DeepMind chair Demis Hassabis said on Wednesday. Speaking at an AI conference in Dublin, Hassabis described recent incidents as “early warning shots” fired by systems that “aren’t that powerful yet”. “So the incidents aren’t that major,” he said. “But they could be, looking into next year and the next couple of years, if we don’t do more work as an industry and individually as companies and governments on securing these systems,” Hassabis warned. Concerns about AI safety have soared after models developed by OpenAI and Anthropic were involved in security incidents during testing, piling on pressure to regulate the technology. Hassabis said new AI models should probably first be tested in offline “sandboxes”, after other companies’ models escaped the closed environments used to assess their capabilities. The European Union’s tech chief, Henna Virkkunen, said AI firms needed to invest more time into testing their systems to retain control over them. “The competition is so hard globally that it seems that all the companies, they are not investing enough time and resources really to test their models,” Virkkunen told reporters as she arrived at the Dublin summit. “They have to be able to control… these systems,” she said, noting that the European Union has sent information requests to all major AI companies asking what safety and security measures they have in place. The European Commission gained new regulatory powers in August under the AI Act, the world’s most far-reaching rules to curb potentially dangerous uses of the technology.

items.title: Aklerh returns to reggae roots with new single ‘Wo Dor’
items.description: Dancehall Queen Aklerh is returning to her reggae roots with Wo Dor , a new lovers’ rock single scheduled for release on Monday, 19 October, under the Revolution Records label. After two Afrobeat hits that grew her audience and showed a playful new side, Aklerh is returning to the reggae dancehall and lovers’ rock sound that first shaped her voice. Wo Dor , which means ‘My Love’, is a lovers’ rock slow burn, featuring soft, melodic rhythms, mellow bass and harmonies that complement Aklerh’s honeyed vocals. It is the kind of song that feels like a late-night conversation with someone you care about: simple, honest and full of feeling. “After exploring afrobeat in my last two singles, Wo Dor is a return to what first inspired me,” Aklerh says. “It’s a demonstration of my versatility: my ability to swing between various genres and freely express my creativity.” “Tubhani Music did well with this song, which marks my return to reggae,” Aklerh adds. “‘Wo Dor’ captures the authenticity of lovers rock while highlighting my journey as an artist: it’s soulful, timeless, and sure to connect with listeners across generations.” Her previous Afrobeat singles, Amele and Good Vibes , showcased Aklerh’s ability to move crowds with contemporary rhythms and groovy hooks. With Wo Dor , she slows the tempo and embraces a timeless warmth, offering longtime fans and new listeners a tender, melodic counterpoint to her dancehall and Afrobeat work. Known for her electrifying performances, Dancehall Queen Aklerh continues to bridge modern sounds and musical tradition, making songs that move both feet and heart.

items.title: KNN demands justice for slain NDC supporter in Enugu
items.description: …Seeks release of Nkanu attack recorder, independent probe into political violence … Says Obi-Kwankwaso presidential project irrepressible By Steve Oko The South-East chapter of the Kwankwaso National Network (KNN) has demanded justice for Christopher Nworie, an alleged supporter of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) reportedly killed during an attack on party members in Enugu State. The group called for the arrest and prosecution of those found responsible for the incident, which reportedly left several other people with gunshot wounds. It also demanded the release of a young man reportedly arrested after recording a separate attack on NDC members in Nkanu, urging security agencies to investigate the incidents and other reported cases of political violence in the state. Nworie, said to be from Affa in Udi Local Government Area, was reportedly killed when suspected political thugs attacked party members at two locations in Enugu on October 10: the Akanu Ibiam Stadium, Emene, and the party’s office in the Government Reserved Area (GRA). The victims had gathered to receive the party’s governorship candidate when the incidents allegedly occurred. In a statement made available to Vanguard in Umuahia, the group’s Zonal Coordinator, Dr Ukpai Iro Ukpai, condemned the reported attacks and called for an independent panel of inquiry to investigate the incidents and other alleged cases of political violence in the state. The group expressed concern that citizens attending political gatherings could allegedly be attacked in broad daylight, insisting that anyone found culpable must face the law. “We are shocked that unarmed and peace-loving citizens, including members of an opposition party, could come under attack in broad daylight while those responsible are yet to be brought to justice. “Every Nigerian has the constitutional right to belong to a political party, attend political meetings and support a candidate of their choice without fear of being attacked, injured or killed. No political ambition is worth the life of any Nigerian,” KNN said. Seeks release of Nkanu attack recorder KNN also expressed concern over the reported arrest and detention of a young man who allegedly recorded an attack on NDC members during a meeting in Nkanu. The video of the incident has since circulated widely on social media. The group called for his immediate release if there was no lawful basis for his continued detention. It also urged the police to clarify the circumstances of his arrest and ensure that investigations established the facts surrounding the reported attack. “If a citizen who records an alleged attack becomes a target of arrest while those accused of perpetrating the violence remain at large, it raises serious questions about the protection of witnesses and the handling of evidence in politically sensitive cases,” the statement said. The group warned that intimidating people who document political violence could discourage witnesses from coming forward, deprive investigators of potentially crucial evidence and undermine efforts to hold perpetrators accountable. It urged the Enugu State Government to address reported incidents of political violence, protect opposition supporters and ensure that political competition was conducted through peaceful engagement and the ballot box. KNN claimed that Enugu had been peaceful before the All Progressives Congress (APC) took control of the state. “Enugu has been a peaceful state and must remain so. The takeover of the state by the APC should not mean the birth of political violence. “The ultimate responsibility of government is the protection of lives and property, irrespective of the political party to which a citizen belongs,” the group said. It warned that unchecked political thuggery could restrict freedom of association, discourage political participation and erode public confidence in the electoral process. The group called on the state government and security agencies to act swiftly and impartially, stressing that citizens must be able to support opposition parties without fear. “Democracy cannot thrive outside opposition. The government must demonstrate that Enugu belongs to all its citizens, not just members or supporters of the ruling party,” the statement said. KNN further urged the state government to take concrete measures to protect opposition members and prevent further attacks. Obi-Kwankwaso project irrepressible — KNN Despite the reported attacks, KNN declared that violence and intimidation would not derail the presidential project of Peter Obi and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, on the NDC platform. Describing the Obi-Kwankwaso project as an “irrepressible national movement fuelled by genuine desire for change”, the group said Nigerians’ determination to shape the country’s future would not be extinguished by political intimidation. It said supporters of the presidential ticket remained committed to what it described as a national movement to rescue the country from political hijackers, insisting that Nigerians must be free to support candidates of their choice. KNN urged the state government, police and other security agencies to investigate the reported attacks, prosecute anyone found culpable and take steps to prevent further political violence in Enugu State. It also called on Nigerians, particularly opposition supporters, not to be intimidated or deterred from exercising their civic rights. The post KNN demands justice for slain NDC supporter in Enugu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 148 kg de cannabis découverts, trois individus interpellés
items.description: La police nationale ivoirienne a annoncé, ce mercredi 14 octobre 2026, l’interpellation de trois individus à Grand-Bassam, après la découverte de 148 kg de cannabis dans deux véhicules de transport avec chauffeur (VTC), dans le cadre de l’opération Épervier Spécial. Un renseignement faisant état du transport de stupéfiants à bord de véhicules de type VTC a conduit le Groupe de répression anti-drogue (GRAD) d’Aboisso à déployer un dispositif de contrôle dans la commune de Grand-Bassam. L’opération a permis d’intercepter deux véhicules. La fouille de leurs coffres a révélé la présence de quatre colis contenant, au total, 148 kilogrammes de cannabis. Trois individus qui se trouvaient à bord ont été interpellés. Il s’agit de G.A., âgé de 47 ans, E.K., 33 ans, et A.K.T., 36 ans. Outre les produits stupéfiants, les forces de l’ordre ont saisi les deux véhicules utilisés pour leur transport présumé. Cette intervention s’inscrit dans le cadre des actions menées par la police ivoirienne contre le trafic de drogues. Les responsabilités des personnes interpellées restent à établir dans le cadre de la procédure judiciaire. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article 148 kg de cannabis découverts, trois individus interpellés est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Tinubu clearing mess you left in Nigerian Airways, Keyamo slams Atiku
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo SAN on Wednesday disclosed that President Bola Tinubu is clearing the mess former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar left behind in the liquidation of Nigeria Airways. Keyamo who made the claim in a post on his X account, accused Atiku of “hypocrisy at its peak.” Her said the President has released N36 billion to settle workers’ unpaid entitlements. He was reacting to a message by Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress ADC, who blamed the Tinubu administration for the rising cost of living in the country. Atiku said “Bola made life expensive” and promised: “I will work to make life affordable again.” He also urged registered voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards PVCs. Keyamo said he would speak only on the sector he heads. “Let me just talk only about the sector that I head, Aviation,” he wrote. He recalled that “In September, 2004, when you were Vice-President, your Government woke up one morning and liquidated Nigeria Airways, throwing thousands of Nigerian[s] out of jobs and into sorrow and pain.” The minister said the workers’ suffering did not end there. “To add salt into their wounds, you refused to pay them their pensions and gratuities, running into billions of Naira,” he said. According to him, Tinubu has now taken on the debt. “Twenty-two years later, after many of them have died out of frustration, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is now clearing the mess you left behind. “Over a month ago, Mr President approved and released the total sum N36 billion to bring succour to these families. They have started receiving alerts and praying for Mr. President. In fact, the President was given an Award for this by the workers’ union a few weeks ago. Yet you sit down there and pontificate? It is only the younger ones who don’t know your history you can attempt to hoodwink, but we will expose you to them. You cannot disguise your inordinate ambition in a cloud of rhetorical gibberish.” The minister also accused Atiku of picking and choosing when to own the record of the government he served in under former President Olusegun Obasanjo. “When it is convenient for you, you claim some credit of the Obasanjo-Atiku government and when not convenient, you say Obasanjo was in charge and not you as Vice-President. The proper posturing of a con artist!” Keyamo said. The post Tinubu clearing mess you left in Nigerian Airways, Keyamo slams Atiku appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Top leaders of India's Cockroach Janta Party sent to jail after protest
items.description: Two leaders of India’s youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) were remanded in custody for five days on Wednesday, as police ratcheted up efforts to clamp down on anti-election commission protests. CJP activists and opposition parties have defied a security crackdown to demand the resignation of India’s chief election commissioner, accusing the poll body of manipulating voter rolls to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling party. The commission, which oversees voting in the world’s most populous nation, has denied any wrongdoing. Delhi police said CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka, 30, and Saurav Das, 27, were taken into custody for their “alleged repeated attempts to disturb public peace and violate the law”. At the end of the five-day remand period, they could have their detention extended, be granted bail or be released. On Tuesday, the pair jumped security barricades to wave the national flag at Jantar Mantar, a decades-old protest site that police have barred people from using. “Their alleged attempts to instigate others through social media to engage in similar unlawful activities were also taken into consideration,” police added. Parliamentary opposition leader Rahul Gandhi, from the Congress party, backed the men, who were detained after entering the site. Jantar Mantar, in the heart of the capital, has been sealed off for days with yellow metal barricades and guarded by security personnel. Delhi Police said on Monday it had removed the site from the list of designated protest venues. ‘Stand up’ “Waving the Tricolour at Jantar Mantar in a peaceful protest is not a crime,” Gandhi said in a post on social media. “Jailing youth for it is an act of cowardice.” The Congress and CJP have both organised protests over the voter roll revision. Gandhi said on Wednesday that “all protests are one”. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke praised the men, saying they “knew they could be thrown behind bars” but went ahead to wave the national flag. “They’ve shown the entire country that the only way to stand up to a bully like Modi is to never bow down, no matter the consequences,” he said in a post on X. Das has worked as a journalist, while Ranka, an engineer, studied at the prestigious Indian Institute of Technology and the London School of Economics. Rights advocates and critics say Modi’s government has eroded democratic freedoms during more than a decade in power, citing pressure on journalists, civil society groups and political opponents – allegations the government rejects. Human Rights Watch said Wednesday the Indian government must uphold the right of citizens to protest peacefully. “The Modi government should stop throwing young protesters in jail and instead engage with them to address concerns over the right to vote and fairness of elections,” it said in a statement. One of the protesters, who gave only her first name, said Wednesday she was taken to a detention centre where she was beaten by police. ‘Unacceptable’ “They punched me here,” said Atira, pointing to her face at a news conference in Delhi, standing next to Gandhi. “I begged them to stop, but then they started kicking me in my private parts, lower abdomen, and back. They didn’t consider me as a human.” AFP could not immediately verify her claim. Journalists in New Delhi marched on Tuesday to protest the detention of reporters during demonstrations. The Press Club of India said any attacks on journalists doing their jobs were “unacceptable”. The electoral list revision, which began last year, has led to more than 133 million names being removed from voter rolls, according to media reports. Critics say the exercise has disproportionately affected minorities, particularly Muslims. Election authorities say the move was intended to eliminate duplicate, deceased and fraudulent entries. Members of Modi’s Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India’s electoral rolls. Home Minister Amit Shah, Modi’s powerful right-hand man, dismissed the protests as localised and accused Gandhi of pursuing an “action plan to protect infiltrators”. “The people of India are not going to fall for your deception,” he said, predicting a “resounding majority” for government in the next general election, due in 2029.

items.title: KP police administrative staff not entitled to risk allowance, rules FCC
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) ruled on Wednesday that the administrative staff of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa police were not entitled to risk allowance. The judgement was issued by a two-member bench headed by Justice Aamer Farooq and including Justice Syed Arshad Hussain Shah. In its ruling, the bench set aside an April 10, 2025 order of the Peshawar High Court’s (PHC) Mingora Bench (Dar-ul-Qaza), Swat, which had granted the police force’s administrative/ministerial staff the benefit. The judgement, authored by Justice Farooq, stated that there was a clear distinction between “uniformed police personnel” performing active operational duties involving risks and hazards and administrative/ministerial staff working in the same department under the KP Police Act, 2017, as well as the KP Police Department Ministerial Service Rules, 1974. The question before the FCC was whether the respondents qualified as police officials entitled to the allowance under the relevant laws or whether a distinction existed between uniformed police personnel and administrative/ministerial staff. The respondents, who were employees of the KP Police establishment, claimed entitlement to risk allowance on the grounds that it was being paid to other employees and staff of the department and that denying them the benefit amounted to discriminatory treatment in violation of Article 25 of the Constitution, which guarantees equality. After the police department denied the grant of the allowance, the respondents challenged the decision before the PHC, which allowed their petition. In its judgement, the FCC observed that administrative/ministerial staff had their own set of rules governing their terms and conditions of service. Under the relevant rules, the FCC stated, such employees had their own method of recruitment, eligibility and composition of service. “Nowhere was it provided that a person appointed as ministerial staff under the rules will be expected to perform active police service,” the judgement said. It added that it was a settled constitutional principle that the guarantee of equality did not mean that all persons must invariably be treated alike, irrespective of the nature of their duties, responsibilities, classifications or conditions of service. The court observed that while Article 25 of the Constitution prohibited discrimination, it did not prevent reasonable classification based on “intelligible differentia having a rational nexus to the object”. “In the case at hand, there exists a clear distinction between uniformed police personnel performing active and operational duties and employees forming part of ministerial establishment,” the court noted, adding that the former may be required to perform duties involving physical danger, law and order operations, arrests, raids, security assignments, crime control and other functions associated with active policing, whereas the latter performed administrative, clerical and ministerial functions. The fact that both the categories were administratively associated with the police department did not obliterate material distinction in the nature of their duties, the judgement said, further stating that the “allowance, which was sanctioned on account of nature, character and hazards of a particular duty, cannot automatically be claimed by every employee serving in the same department”. “The high court appears to have proceeded primarily on the fact that both categories of employees are serving in the police department,” the FCC noted. “Such an approach did not adequately address the material distinction in their relevant service functions,” the judgement said. The FCC observed that the respondents had essentially sought parity on the basis of departmental affiliation. “Such a claim cannot succeed unless basic requirement of similarity of duties and service conditions is established,” the FCC emphasised. “The constitutional prohibition against discrimination does not require the state to treat the dissimilar classes although they are identical.” The judgement concluded that the high court “fell into error” in allowing the writ petition merely on the basis of alleged discrimination without examining whether the respondents were similarly placed with the employees who were being paid the risk allowance and whether the classification made by the government had a rational basis. Dismissing the plea, the FCC observed that the denial of the allowance to the respondents did not constitute hostile discrimination or offend constitutional guarantees of equality.

items.title: Lagos-Calabar highway, rail link to ease students’ travel — NANS
items.description: By Adeola Badru The National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS) has said the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and its accompanying rail system will improve students’ mobility, reduce travel time and ease access to tertiary institutions across the South-West and South-South regions. The association said the Federal Government’s coastal highway project would strengthen connectivity between geopolitical zones, facilitate the movement of people and goods, and create economic opportunities across the country. NANS President, Akinteye Babatunde Afeez, stated this after leading a delegation of the association on an inspection of the highway as part of its nationwide federal roads project tour. Afeez, in a statement, described the project as a major infrastructure investment with far-reaching implications for transportation, commerce and national development. “I must say that we are impressed by the sheer scale of this project. The Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is not an ordinary road construction project. “The massive bridges, the scale of the construction and the foresight behind the project reflect the Federal Government’s remarkable investment in infrastructural development,” he said. He said the highway’s benefits would extend beyond road transportation, noting that its completion was expected to improve connectivity, ease the movement of people and goods, and strengthen commercial activities across geopolitical zones. “Beyond the impressive outlook, the economic value of this highway cannot be overemphasised. Upon completion, it is expected to improve connectivity, ease the movement of people and goods, open up economic opportunities and strengthen commercial activities across geopolitical zones. “The most impressive part of it is the rail system that comes with the road,” Afeez said. The NANS president said students were among those expected to benefit from improved transportation infrastructure, particularly those who travel long distances to pursue their studies in institutions across the country. “As the apex body representing Nigerian students, our interest in this project goes beyond the quality of the construction. “We are particularly concerned about how the infrastructure of this magnitude will improve the welfare and mobility of our students. “Many Nigerian students travel from different parts of the country to pursue their academic programmes in institutions across the South-South and South-West,” he said. According to him, improved connectivity between the two regions would reduce the time students spend travelling to their campuses, make journeys less stressful and improve access to educational institutions. “This is equally important, as students will not have to travel for hours before connecting to their campuses in either the South-West or the South-South,” he added. Afeez commended President Bola Tinubu’s administration for its infrastructure development agenda and acknowledged the role of the Minister of Works, David Umahi, in driving the coastal highway project. “We therefore commend President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, for the commitment of his administration to major infrastructure development, as well as the Honourable Minister of Works, Engr. David Umahi, CON, for the drive and foresight behind this unprecedented landmark project,” he said. He described quality infrastructure as a critical driver of national development, adding that students stood to benefit from investments that improve mobility and access to educational opportunities. “Quality infrastructure is essential to national development, of which Nigerian students are major beneficiaries,” Afeez said. He said NANS would continue its nationwide federal roads project tour to assess roads leading to tertiary institutions and provide independent observations and recommendations where necessary. “As we continue our Nationwide Federal Roads Project Tour, we remain committed to assessing federal roads leading to our campuses and offering our unbiased commendations and recommendations where necessary,” he said. The post Lagos-Calabar highway, rail link to ease students’ travel — NANS appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Stacy Mense’s ‘W’ahyira Me’ gains airplay on radio, digital platforms
items.description: Ghanaian contemporary gospel artiste Stacy Mense is gaining attention with her debut single, W’ahyira Me , which has received airplay and is performing well on digital platforms. The song speaks of God’s goodness and the blessings that come with trust in and obedience to His word. Stacy Mense, born Anastasia Hannah Amuzu, is a Ghanaian contemporary gospel artiste, singer, songwriter, worship leader and registered nurse whose life and artistry are deeply rooted in faith, worship, service and a desire to inspire others through music. Her musical journey began in childhood and has evolved through years of church worship, gospel ministry, songwriting, vocal performance and service. Today, Stacy brings together heartfelt worship, personal testimony and contemporary gospel expression to create music that glorifies God while encouraging listeners to remain anchored in faith, hope, gratitude and the promises of God. THE ARTIST For Stacy Mense, music is more than creative expression; it is an extension of her faith and a form of ministry. Her musical journey began at an early age, singing alto alongside her siblings as part of a family singing band within a well-established family fellowship. This early exposure to music nurtured her vocal ability and established a lasting passion for worship and gospel music. That foundation continued to develop through her involvement in church ministry. Stacy became an active member of The Church of Pentecost, Avenor Branch, where she served on the worship team and ministered during Sunday services. Through this experience, she began to understand worship not simply as music, but as an opportunity to serve God and His people. She later became a member of the gospel trio Victorious Sisters, founded by Christopher Baffour Awuah, the younger brother of Reverend Owusu Ansah. The group was managed by Reverend Gabriel Ansah and Mr Kankam and featured Stacy alongside Esther Saforo and the late Cynthia Tetteh. Stacy’s musical development continued through her involvement with gospel music groups, including One Family and Marko and the Urban Worshippers, where she contributed as both a singer and songwriter. She has written songs for these groups as well as for individual gospel artistes, including Nicole King. Her experience also extends to backing vocals and collaborative gospel ministry. She has ministered alongside Ghanaian gospel musicians, including the late Sampson Annor and Nana Yaw Asare. Her engagements included a performance of Nana Yaw Asare’s Odumankoma during the launch of the All-Gospel Stars song in Kumasi. These experiences have played an important role in shaping Stacy’s development as a vocalist, songwriter, worship minister and contemporary gospel artiste. A LIFE ROOTED IN WORSHIP Stacy’s ministry journey has continued across several Christian communities, each contributing to her spiritual growth and development as a worshipper and servant of God. She was a committed member of International Central Gospel Church (ICGC), Osu Branch, where she worshipped under the ministry of Rev. Kofi Okyere, now the resident pastor of ICGC Milton Keynes Branch. She later became a member of ICGC Tesano Branch, which was more convenient to her place of residence. There, she worshipped under the leadership of Rev. Gabriel Dela during a significant period of her life before marriage and her relocation abroad. Stacy currently worships with Lighthouse Chapel International (Mustard Seed Chapel International), Liverpool Branch, where she served as a praise and worship leader under the ministry of Rev. Kenneth Abubakr. Her commitment to ministry extends beyond music and worship. Through her involvement with the children’s ministry at Save Church within Mustard Seed Chapel International, Stacy has also developed a heart for nurturing, encouraging and positively influencing the next generation. Whenever she visits Ghana, she continues to worship with ICGC The New Wine Temple under the leadership of Rev. Albert Ocran, maintaining a meaningful connection with the Christian community and spiritual heritage that have contributed to her journey. For Stacy, worship extends far beyond the microphone. It is expressed through service, encouragement, mentorship, compassion and a willingness to make a positive difference in the lives of others. ‘W’AHYIRA ME’: THE DEBUT On 13 July 2026, Stacy Mense entered a defining new chapter in her musical journey with the release of her debut official single, W’ahyira Me . The song is a heartfelt declaration of God’s goodness, faithfulness and blessings through every season and circumstance of life. Drawing from her personal faith and testimony, Stacy uses the song to acknowledge God’s hand throughout her journey while reminding listeners of His unwavering presence, love and faithfulness. More than simply a debut release, W’ahyira Me represents a statement of faith and the beginning of Stacy’s public recorded music ministry. Through the song, she encourages listeners to recognise God’s goodness even in challenging seasons, remain hopeful through adversity and celebrate His blessings with gratitude. The release represents not only a new musical beginning, but also the culmination of years of worship, preparation, personal growth, ministry and faith. MUSIC WITH PURPOSE Stacy’s musical identity is centred on authenticity, faith and purpose. Her artistry explores themes of God’s faithfulness, gratitude, hope, perseverance, testimony, worship and divine goodness. Through her distinctive voice and heartfelt delivery, she seeks to communicate messages that are both deeply personal and spiritually uplifting. Rather than viewing music solely as entertainment, Stacy sees gospel music as an opportunity to create moments of reflection, worship, encouragement, healing and connection with God. Her aspiration is to create music that speaks to people wherever they may be in their journey, whether they are celebrating a breakthrough, navigating a difficult season, searching for encouragement or simply longing to draw closer to God. At the heart of her artistry is a simple conviction: music can become a vessel through which faith is strengthened, hope is restored and lives are encouraged. THE HEART BEHIND THE MUSIC Alongside her musical ministry, Stacy is a registered nurse, a profession that reflects another important dimension of her commitment to serving others. Her nursing career has strengthened qualities such as compassion, empathy, patience, attentiveness, responsibility and genuine care for people. These qualities naturally influence the way she approaches music and ministry. For Stacy, caring for people through nursing and encouraging people through music are complementary expressions of service. Both allow her to connect with others, offer support, provide encouragement and contribute positively to their lives. This intersection of healthcare, faith, ministry, worship and music gives Stacy a distinctive perspective as an emerging contemporary gospel artiste. Her experiences have taught her that people need more than words: they need hope, compassion, reassurance and reminders that they are not alone. These values continue to influence the message she carries through her music. THE JOURNEY AHEAD Stacy Mense stands at the beginning of a new chapter in her musical career. From singing alto alongside her siblings as a young girl to serving in church worship teams, participating in gospel music groups, writing songs, leading praise and worship, serving children and ultimately releasing her first official single, her journey has been shaped by one consistent thread: faith expressed through service and music. Her debut single, W’ahyira Me , marks the beginning of her recorded music journey while representing the culmination of years of worship, ministry, personal development and preparation. As she continues to develop her artistry, Stacy remains committed to creating music that is authentic, uplifting, inspirational, worshipful and centred on God. Her vision is to reach wider audiences, share her testimony through music, encourage people through every season of life and use her God-given gifts to make a meaningful spiritual impact. With a heart for worship, a passion for people and a growing musical voice, Stacy Mense is stepping into this new chapter with faith, purpose, humility and gratitude, trusting God to guide every step of the journey.

items.title: CHU de Tanger : une enquête ouverte après des complications oculaires chez 15 patients diabétiques
items.description: Une commission d’enquête relevant du ministère de la Santé et de la Protection sociale mène actuellement des investigations au Centre hospitalier universitaire (CHU) Mohammed VI de Tanger, à la suite d’un incident ayant causé de graves troubles de la vision, allant jusqu’à la perte de la vue, chez 15 patients diabétiques, ont révélé des sources bien informées à Hespress. Ces derniers avaient reçu des injections dans le cadre de leur suivi médical régulier au service d’ophtalmologie et de chirurgie ophtalmologique de l’établissement. Selon les mêmes sources, une enquête approfondie a été ouverte après l’apparition de cas d’inflammation aiguë chez deux patients, à la suite d’un traitement médical reçu le 8 octobre courant. L’hôpital a alors contacté les patients ayant bénéficié du même traitement, au nombre de 18. Il s’est avéré que la majorité d’entre eux présentaient des symptômes similaires, soulevant ainsi de nombreuses interrogations sur les circonstances de cet incident. Les mêmes informations indiquent que la commission de lutte contre les infections ainsi que l’Agence nationale du sang se sont rendues à l’hôpital. Des prélèvements sanguins ont été effectués sur les patients atteints d’inflammation aiguë afin de réaliser les examens et analyses nécessaires pour déterminer les causes réelles de ces inflammations, qui ont entraîné chez certains patients une perte presque totale de la vue. Les mêmes sources précisent que la majorité des patients ayant développé des complications à la suite de l’injection administrée au niveau de l’œil sont des personnes âgées diabétiques. Ils souffraient déjà d’une baisse de la vision liée aux complications de cette maladie chronique, ainsi que d’une fragilité de la rétine. Une source responsable au sein de l’hôpital, ayant requis l’anonymat, a indiqué que les dossiers médicaux des patients atteints d’inflammation aiguë à la suite de l’injection en question montrent que leur acuité visuelle était, dans tous les cas, d’environ 2/10. Cette faiblesse visuelle préexistante a accentué les effets de l’inflammation aiguë sur leur vision, au point que certains ont eu le sentiment d’avoir totalement perdu la vue. La même source a précisé que des équipes médicales spécialisées assurent la prise en charge et le suivi de l’ensemble des cas recensés au sein du CHU, soulignant que l’évolution définitive de leur état ne pourra être déterminée qu’au bout d’environ trois mois. Concernant les interrogations sur les causes de l’inflammation aiguë et sur une éventuelle péremption des injections administrées aux patients, la source responsable a écarté l’hypothèse de médicaments périmés. « Le médicament n’est pas périmé et sa date de validité court jusqu’au 30 septembre 2028 », a-t-elle affirmé. La même source a souligné que les enquêtes et investigations en cours permettront de déterminer si l’inflammation aiguë observée chez les patients ayant reçu le traitement est due à « une modification chimique de la composition du médicament ou à d’autres infections ». Elle a également relevé que plusieurs de ces patients avaient déjà reçu la même injection à cinq reprises dans le cadre de leur protocole thérapeutique. items.title: Economic activities mixed in 7 months of 2026; Cement sales decline by 10%
items.description: Consumer spending, proxied by domestic VAT collections and retail sales, posted a mixed performance in July 2026, compared with the corresponding period in 2025, the September 2026 Monetary Policy Report. Domestic VAT collections increased by 11.5% on a year-on year basis to GH¢2.142 billion, from GH¢1.922 billion. Cumulatively, total domestic VAT for the first seven months of 2026 went up by 13.8% to GH¢13.617 billion compared with GH¢11.965 billion for the corresponding period of last year. Retail sales, however, declined by 1.5% (year-on-year) to GH¢236.41 million in July 2026, down from the GH¢239.89 million recorded in the same period in 2025. On a month-on-month basis, retail sales moderated by 0.8% in July 2026 from GH¢238.25 million in the preceding month. In cumulative terms, retail sales for the first seven months of 2026 went up by 2.2 percent compared to the same period of last year. Manufacturing Activities Also, activities in the manufacturing sub-sector, gauged by trends in the collection of direct taxes and private sector workers’ contributions to the Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) Pension Scheme (Tier-1), improved in July 2026. The total direct taxes collected increased by 53.5% (year-on-year) to GH¢8.085 billion in July 2026, relative to GH¢5.265 billion recorded in the corresponding period in 2025. Cumulatively, total direct taxes collected for the first seven months of 2026 went up by 27.7% to GH¢60.771 billion, from GH¢47.592 billion for the same period in 2025. Als, the total private sector workers’ contribution to the SSNIT Pension Scheme (Tier-1) increased by 11.2% in year-on year terms to GH¢570.59 million in July 2026, from GH¢513.34 million collected during the corresponding period in 2025. Cumulatively, for the first seven months of 2026, the contribution grew by 10.7 percent to GH¢3.856 billion, relative to GH¢3.482 billion recorded in the same period in 2025. Construction Sector Activities Furthermore, activity in the construction sub-sector, proxied by the volume of cement sales, declined by 4.9% (year-on-year) in July 2026 to 202,218.17 tonnes, from 212,735.33 tonnes recorded a year ago. Similarly, on a month-on-month basis, total cement sales moderated by 0.6 percent in July 2026 compared with the 203,435.35 tonnes recorded in June 2026. Cumulatively, cement sales for the first seven months of 2026 declined by 10.3 percent to 1,475,115.01 tonnes, from 1,644,413.19 tonnes for the same period of 2025. According to the report, the relative decline in total cement sales, year-on-year, was due to a moderation in construction activities during the review period. Vehicle Registration For vehicle registration, transport sector activities, gauged by new vehicle registrations by the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA), improved by 51.7% to 31,909 in July 2026, from 21,038 vehicles registered during the corresponding period of 2025. Cumulatively, the number of vehicles registered by the DVLA within the first seven months of 2026 increased by 52.7% to 228,261 from 149,440 recorded a year ago.

items.title: Tragedy averted as 33,000-litre ethanol truck falls off Lagos bridge
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — A major disaster was averted on Wednesday after a truck conveying 33,000 litres of ethanol fell off the Second Rainbow Bridge in the Amuwo Odofin Local Government Area of Lagos State. The Permanent Secretary of the Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA), Dr. Olufemi Oke-Osanyintolu, confirmed the incident, saying no casualty was recorded. The incident, which occurred at about 11am, involved a FOTON truck with registration number APP 346 YC. The truck reportedly fell while the driver was attempting to negotiate a turn on the bridge. According to Oke-Osanyintolu, preliminary investigations attributed the incident to speeding, which caused the truck’s turntable to detach and fall onto the roundabout, obstructing the entire stretch. He said the highly volatile nature of ethanol posed a significant risk of fire and explosion, prompting the immediate deployment of emergency responders. “Recognising the highly volatile nature of ethanol and the imminent risk of fire and explosion, the Eagle Response Team, in collaboration with other responders, immediately cordoned off the area and activated crowd and traffic control measures,” he said. The LASEMA chief added that operatives of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service and the Federal Fire Service promptly applied chemical foam to the truck and the surrounding area to suppress fumes and prevent a secondary incident. Officers of the Nigeria Police Force and the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA) also secured the scene and managed traffic to prevent further danger. “Through coordinated and tactical efforts, a major disaster was averted, and no loss of life or casualty was recorded,” Oke-Osanyintolu said. Cement truck obstructs traffic in Agege In a separate incident, LASEMA said its Tiger Response Team from C3 restored traffic movement at Oke Koto, Agege, after a Dangote cement truck climbed a road divider and became stuck. Oke-Osanyintolu attributed the incident to reckless driving, which obstructed vehicular movement and necessitated the deployment of the response team in collaboration with LASTMA. He said the agency deployed its heavy-duty recovery equipment, known as Super Metro, to remove the truck, which was subsequently towed to the LASTMA yard for further action. The road was reopened to traffic, with no death or injury recorded. The LASEMA chief commended the emergency responders for their swift intervention and urged motorists to observe speed limits and traffic regulations, particularly when transporting heavy loads and hazardous materials. He also advised residents to report emergencies through the agency’s toll-free numbers, 767 and 112. The incidents came a day after emergency responders rescued two men from a fire that engulfed an eight-room bungalow on Onitire Road, Itire, Lagos. During the incident, a 42-year-old man sustained burns while rescuing a 75-year-old wheelchair user. The post Tragedy averted as 33,000-litre ethanol truck falls off Lagos bridge appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le président Tebboune écrit au Pape Léon XIV hospitalisé
items.description: Le président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, a adressé ce mercredi 14 octobre une lettre au pape Léon IXV qui a été hospitalisé pour une opération chirurgicale. «C’est avec une profonde émotion et une grande compassion que j’ai appris votre admission à l’hôpital en vue d’une intervention chirurgicale. Face à cette épreuve de santé, je tiens à vous exprimer mes sincères sentiments de solidarité et de soutien, ainsi que mes vœux les plus chaleureux de réussite de l’intervention chirurgicale, de prompt rétablissement et de pleine santé», a écrit le Président de la République dans son message au souverain pontife. Tebboune écrit au pape Léon XIV atteint d’un cancer du poumon Le pape qui a effectué une historique en Algérie en avril dernier a été admis mardi l'hôpital Gemelli de Rome, pour une intervention chirurgicale afin de lui retirer un nodule pulmonaire. Une opération considérée peu risquée par les spécialistes. Le Vatican a révélé que le pape, 71 ans, est atteint d’un cancer du poumon et doit subir des examens complémentaires. Applausi e affetto per #LeoneXIV , arrivato alle 13.07 al #PoliclinicoGemelli per l’intervento di rimozione di un nodulo al polmone. La folla, presente fin dal mattino, augura al Papa una pronta guarigione: “Siamo con te, vinci questa battaglia!”. leggi: https://t.co/QCdQ2DvwxY pic.twitter.com/2uJph1UP1j — Vatican News (@vaticannews_it) October 13, 2026 Dans son message, le président Tebboune a salué les efforts de Léon XIV en « faveur de la promotion des valeurs de paix et de tolérance à travers le monde », et formé le vœu que le pape retrouve sa « pleine santé dans les meilleurs délais, afin de « poursuivre votre action au service du renforcement du dialogue et de la compréhension entre les peuples ». L’article Le président Tebboune écrit au Pape Léon XIV hospitalisé est apparu en premier sur TSA .
