items.title: ABUAD: Canadian, US varsities to award Afe Babalola honorary law degrees
items.description: …Varsity to honour Cavista Holdings chairman, two others as 286 students bag first-class degrees By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — The Founder and Chancellor of Afe Babalola University, Ado-Ekiti (ABUAD), Aare Afe Babalola, will receive honorary Doctor of Laws degrees from two foreign universities as the institution prepares to graduate 2,194 students at its 14th convocation ceremonies. Trinity Western University, Canada, and Trinity International University, United States, will confer the honours on Babalola during the grand finale of the convocation scheduled for October 21, 2026. The Vice-Chancellor of ABUAD, Prof. Smaranda Olarinde, disclosed this on Wednesday at a press conference to announce activities for the university’s 14th convocation, scheduled to run from October 14 to 21. Olarinde said the honorary degrees recognised Babalola’s contributions to legal scholarship, educational innovation, philanthropy, social development and leadership. She said the international recognition underscored the impact of his investments in education and institution-building, as well as his longstanding commitment to public service. In a related development, the university will confer honorary Doctor of Letters degrees, honoris causa, on three Nigerians: the Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Prof. Obiora Okonkwo; Chairman of Cavista Holdings, John Olajide; and business leader, Dr. Rosemary Osula Mku-Atu. The vice-chancellor said the awards were intended to recognise the recipients’ contributions to society and provide graduating students with examples of how professional accomplishments could be matched with service to humanity. According to her, Okonkwo will be honoured for his contributions to enterprise, philanthropy and the advancement of quality, functional education. Olajide will receive the award in recognition of his investments in enterprise and support for healthcare, education, poverty alleviation and women’s empowerment, while Mku-Atu will be recognised for her commitment to supporting the less privileged and promoting quality education. Meanwhile, 2,194 students are expected to graduate at the convocation, making the Class of 2026 the largest graduating cohort since the university commenced academic activities in January 2010. Of the total, 1,759 students completed undergraduate and professional programmes, while 435 are graduating from postgraduate programmes. The postgraduate figure comprises 359 students from the College of Postgraduate Studies and 76 from the ABUAD Business School’s postgraduate programmes. Olarinde disclosed that 286 graduands obtained first-class degrees, while 824 earned second-class upper degrees. Another 234 students obtained second-class lower degrees, while 29 graduated with third-class degrees. The remaining graduands completed professional or postgraduate programmes to which the conventional undergraduate degree classifications do not apply. The vice-chancellor also announced that Okonkwo would deliver the convocation lecture titled, “Functional Education and the Nigeria Project: Strategic Human Capital Development for National Renewal”. She said the topic was relevant to Nigeria’s development needs, particularly the importance of an education system that equips graduates with knowledge, character and practical skills to create value, solve problems and contribute to national development. Olarinde said the honorary degrees for Babalola further highlighted the international recognition of his commitment to institution-building and service to humanity. “His insistence that education must solve problems and improve society is reflected in our teaching, professional training, research, farms, industrial park, the ABUAD Multisystem Hospital, community engagements and international partnerships,” she said. She noted that the university’s graduating class had grown from 103 students at its inaugural convocation in 2013 to 2,194 in 2026. Addressing the graduands, Olarinde said their certificates carried both honour and responsibility, urging them to uphold competence, discipline, ethical conduct and integrity in their professional and personal lives. “The value of your education will be measured not only by the positions you occupy, but by the problems you solve, the people you serve and the integrity with which you conduct yourselves,” she said. She stressed that investment in universities was essential to national development, noting that education played a critical role in healthcare, food security, technology, enterprise, public administration, security and national stability. The vice-chancellor reaffirmed the university’s commitment to developing graduates equipped with knowledge, practical skills and sound moral values to create opportunities and serve their communities. items.title: GFA and Sports Ministry must not rush Black Stars head coach appointment – Nana Fitz
items.description: Veteran football administrator Fitzgerald Barkers Woode has cautioned the Ghana Football Association (GFA) against rushing the appointment of a new head coach for the Black Stars. His advice comes following Carlos Queiroz’s mutual exit after Ghana’s humiliating start to the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers. The Black Stars suffered a 2–0 defeat to Côte d’Ivoire in Bouaké, followed by a disappointing 4–2 loss to The Gambia on home soil. Following Queiroz’s departure, the GFA and the Ministry of Youth and Sports established a five-member search committee to evaluate, interview, and shortlist potential candidates for the vacant post. The GFA set October 15 as the deadline for applications. Ghana is scheduled to face Somalia in a back-to-back qualifier this November at the Accra Sports Stadium. An interim technical crew is expected to manage the team through those fixtures before a substantive manager is formally appointed. Speaking to Graphic Sports, Barkers Woode popularly known as Nana Fitz urged the football authorities to remain patient during the hiring process despite the mounting pressure to turn the team’s form around. Nana Fitz stressed that the next head coach must possess a deep understanding of Ghanaian football, its unique challenges, and the cultural context surrounding the national team. According to him, the GFA needs to appoint someone who truly recognizes our local football environment, the country’s footballing philosophy, and the realities of the resources available. Nana Fitz noted that such insight would help the new coach adapt swiftly and deliver the expected results. The Black Stars currently sit at the bottom of Group C without a point.

items.title: FCC rejects Bushra Bibi's petition seeking suspension of 7-year Al-Qadir Trust sentence
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) on Wednesday rejected a plea moved by the spouse of incarcerated former premier Imran Khan, Bushra Bibi, seeking suspension of her seven-year sentence in the £190 Al-Qadir Trust case . “We find no sufficient ground warranting interference with the April 30 Islamabad High Court (IHC) order at this stage,” Chief Justice Aminuddin Khan, who headed a two-judge FCC bench, observed. The court also expressed the expectation that the high court would endeavour to decide the main appeal, affording both sides adequate opportunity of hearing while discouraging unnecessary adjournments. Earlier in the day, a two-judge FCC bench comprising the chief justice and Justice Ali Baqar Najafi had reserved its ruling on the plea. Bushra had moved the FCC in July seeking the suspension of her sentence, with her criminal appeal contending that the appellant, being a woman with a serious medical condition, was entitled to the suspension of her sentence. On Sept 17, her counsel moved an application before the FCC, seeking early hearing of the appeal, citing a rapidly deteriorating ocular condition that threatens the appellant’s remaining eyesight. In a three-page order issued on Wednesday, the FCC noted that the application seeking the suspension of the sentence had remained pending before the IHC on account of successive adjournments sought by the National Accountability Bureau (NAB). The FCC said that, without entering into the merits of the application under Section 426 of the Criminal Procedure Code, the IHC had declined to suspend the sentence, principally on the ground that the main appeal had already been fixed for hearing and the appellant’s counsel was not extending the requisite assistance towards its adjudication. The record further reflected that the appeal, initially fixed for April 30, was subsequently adjourned to May 7 and thereafter to Oct 5. The principal grievance urged by counsel representing the appellant pertained to the repeated adjournments allegedly sought by NAB, resulting in the prolongation of proceedings on the application for suspension of sentence, the FCC observed. “Be that as it may, the main appeal having already been fixed for hearing, the appropriate course would be to secure its expeditious adjudication rather than undertake a parallel examination of the merits of suspension of sentence at this stage,” the FCC observed. The appellant’s assertion that the appeal involved a voluminous record necessitating elaborate arguments did not, by itself, furnish sufficient justification for interference with the impugned order, the order said. It was, therefore, incumbent upon the appellant’s counsel to extend full assistance to the IHC in hearing the main appeal, whereafter NAB would be equally obligated to advance its arguments without unnecessary adjournments, the judgment said. The FCC also noted that the present criminal appeal was barred by 61 days, for which the appellant had sought condonation of delay. The explanation furnished, particularly the appellant’s incarceration at Central Jail, Adiala, Rawalpindi, constituted sufficient cause warranting condonation, the FCC observed while condoning the delay of 61 days in filing the appeal. The appeal Moved under Section 32-A of the National Accountability Ordinance read with Article 175F(1)(a) of the Constitution, the criminal appeal pleaded before the FCC that, despite earlier directions issued by the IHC to the authorities of Central Jail Adiala to facilitate a meeting between the appellant and her counsel, the jail authorities were not complying with the directions. Her counsel was instead permitted to meet the appellant’s husband, Imran Khan, who disclosed that both he and the appellant were being illegally kept in solitary confinement. They were allegedly denied access to family, friends, counsel and political party members, as well as to each other, and were not provided with books or television, thereby subjecting them to complete isolation from human contact and depriving them of information about the outside world. The same was subsequently confirmed by the appellant’s daughters upon meeting her after her eye surgery on April 17, the appeal stated. Such treatment amounted to an unauthorised enhancement of sentence, violated the prisoners’ fundamental rights to life and dignity guaranteed under Article 9 of the Constitution, and warranted immediate intervention by the FCC, the petition argued. The appeal stated that the appellant had been subjected to continuous solitary confinement, which had demonstrably taken a grave toll on her physical and mental health. This was evident from the fact that she had to be taken outside the jail premises for eye surgery. In view of her deteriorating medical condition, she ought not to be subjected to solitary confinement even if such punishment had been awarded by a court. However, in blatant disregard of the applicable law and prison rules, she continued to be subjected to such unlawful confinement, the petition pleaded. The appeal contended that NAB had selectively prosecuted the appellant and her husband while deliberately excluding six other individuals who were allegedly implicated in the matter. The core allegations revolved around the Malik Riaz family and other persons who had conspicuously not been subjected to prosecution. This selective and incomplete approach had resulted in a defective and biased investigation, culminating in the unjust framing of charges and subsequent conviction of the appellant, the appeal contended. Thus, the prosecution had failed to present cogent, reliable and legally admissible evidence to substantiate the allegations in their entirety. Earlier this month, senior members of the PTI’s legal team approached the FCC for early fixation of the criminal appeal. However, no fresh application was filed, and only a verbal request was made for early registration and fixation of the case. The former first lady was handed the sentence in the case in January last year, and remains imprisoned at Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail. The court found Imran and Bushra guilty of giving undue favours to property tycoon Riaz in retrieving his laundered money from the United Kingdom. Bushra, along with the ex-PM, had initially moved the Islamabad High Court (IHC) for the suspension of her sentence in July last year. But the high court dismissed their requests in May 2026, observing that their appeals against their convictions had already been fixed for hearing. Subsequently, the two approached the Supreme Court against the IHC decision, but the SC office returned the petition as being not maintainable, explaining that since the IHC had passed the impugned order while exercising jurisdiction under Section 32 of the National Accountability Ordinance (NAO), 1999, the remedy lay exclusively before the FCC under Section 32-A of the ordinance. Bushra then moved the FCC on July 30, with her criminal appeal contending that the appellant, being a woman with a serious medical condition, was entitled to the suspension of her sentence, as similar relief was contemplated under the first proviso to Section 497(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC). Her latest application for the appeal’s early hearing, which was rejected on Monday, also stated that her rapidly deteriorating ocular condition threatened her remaining eyesight.

items.title: Rising debt: IMF urges FG to boost revenue, cut waste
items.description: Backs targeted transport subsidies to cushion Nigerians against fuel costs Recommends more spending on health, education, infrastructure Warns against fiscal measures that worsen cost-of-living crisis By Babajide Komolafe, Economy Editor Bangkok, Thailand: The International Monetary Fund, IMF, has urged the Federal Government to boost revenue mobilisation, eliminate distortions in the tax system and redirect public spending towards growth-enhancing sectors as Nigeria grapples with rising debt and debt-servicing costs. The Fund also backed targeted transport subsidies to cushion vulnerable Nigerians against rising fuel costs, warning that blanket subsidies are expensive and less effective than directing assistance to those who need it most. Rodrigo Valdés, Director, Fiscal Affairs Department, IMF, and Davide Furceri, Division Chief in the department, gave the recommendations at a press briefing on the Fund’s Fiscal Monitor October 2026 report, during the ongoing IMF/World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand. The IMF’s recommendation is at the background of the continued rise in the nation’s public debt in spite of a sharp increase in government revenue. Nigeria’s total public debt rose by 71 per cent to N166.788 trillion at the end of June 2026 from N97.34 trillion at the end of 2023. This was in spite of a sharp increase in government revenue, reflected in the 112 per cent increase in statutory allocation to the three tiers of government to N23.15 trillion in 2025 from N10.9 trillion in 2023. Commenting on Nigeria’s rising debt despite increased revenue following tax reforms and fuel subsidy removal, Valdés cautioned against a blanket approach to fiscal consolidation. “It’s very important to nuance the message of consolidation now, because not all countries are in the same position,” he said. “Many major economies need to start consolidation now. But there are other countries that, let me just mention the UK, where our recommendation is stay the course. We’re not saying accelerate the pace of consolidation.” On the political and economic implications of higher fuel prices, Valdés acknowledged the difficulty of managing the impact on households but argued that governments should avoid spending scarce resources on blanket subsidies. “At the end of the day, it’s very tempting politically speaking because the political effect of the price of oil, of fuels, of gasoline, of diesel is not trivial,” he said. “But you have to explain that this is a growth shock. Second, it’s very, very expensive for the country not to recognise that shock, and third, it’s much better to use some of that money that you would spend on the subsidies, channelled towards more vulnerable people.” He suggested that governments could provide more focused assistance to cushion the impact of higher fuel prices, particularly on public transportation. “Gasoline could go up, and perhaps bus fees may be subsidised in a way. That is a much better policy at the end of the day than just a blanket subsidy for everybody,” Valdés stated. Furceri said Nigeria and other countries with relatively low tax bases needed to mobilise sufficient revenue both to meet rising interest obligations and finance investments that support economic growth. “For many countries that are starting from a very low tax base, and this is, for example, the case of Ethiopia, the case of Nigeria, it’s important to have sufficient revenue for two reasons,” he said. “One, because this revenue will help the countries to pay high interest costs, and second, because it will generate sufficient resources the countries can use to spend on growth.” He, however, stressed that increasing revenue should not be the only objective of tax reform, arguing that better-designed taxes could support growth without necessarily increasing the overall tax burden. “There are many distortions that are in current tax systems. Clearly, removing the distortions can be revenue-neutral, but they can actually increase growth and also address this trade-off,” Furceri said. On expenditure priorities, he urged the Federal Government to redirect resources towards sectors with long-term economic benefits. “Many countries have the scope to reprioritise spending for things that matter for long-term growth. Think about spending on education, spending on health, spending on investment, and, in the current circumstances, to again move away from subsidies to more targeted interventions,” he said. Furceri acknowledged that targeted support could be difficult in countries without comprehensive national registries and digital payment systems. However, he said governments could use alternative mechanisms while building the infrastructure needed for more effective delivery. “Typically, one argument that many countries say is that it’s very difficult to target subsidies because we don’t have a national registry, we have to have digital payment. It is important that countries prepare these systems in the medium term,” he said. “In the short term, there are alternative ways. Rodrigo mentioned one. For example, school feeding is another one. Doing geographical targeting is another one. If countries have vulnerable farmers, there is scope to compensate them.” The recommendations come as the IMF warns of mounting global fiscal risks. Its Fiscal Monitor October 2026 projects that global public debt could reach 100 per cent of gross domestic product by the end of the decade, while higher interest rates are expected to raise government debt-servicing costs as existing obligations are refinanced. The Fund also estimated that measures used to suppress energy prices cost governments approximately 1.5 per cent of global GDP, warning that broad-based subsidies are fiscally expensive and often regressive. It called on governments to improve tax systems, make public expenditure more growth-friendly and undertake fiscal consolidation where necessary, backed by credible plans, stronger institutions and greater transparency. items.title: Nkrumah Showboy: Chief Moomen’s play to explore Ghana’s first President’s early years
items.description: Bambu Heritage Productions will preview Nkrumah Showboy: Part One: The Boy from Nkroful , a new theatre production exploring the early life of Ghana’s first President, Osagyefo Dr Kwame Nkrumah, in Accra on Friday, 16 October 2026. The production, written by celebrated Ghanaian poet and playwright Chief Moomen, will be staged at the National Theatre at 7.30 pm. It takes audiences beyond Nkrumah’s political leadership to explore the formative years, experiences and influences that helped shape the man who would lead Ghana to independence. Part One follows Nkrumah’s journey from his childhood in Nkroful through his education at Achimota and his subsequent experiences at Lincoln University and the University of Pennsylvania in the United States. Through music, drama and dance, the production offers audiences a closer look at a relatively less explored chapter in the life of one of Africa’s most consequential leaders. For Chief Moomen, the production represents a major creative undertaking and forms part of a broader effort to bring Ghana’s history to life through compelling cultural experiences. Nkrumah Showboy is also part of Bambu Heritage Productions’ wider historical storytelling initiative being developed ahead of Ghana’s 70th anniversary of independence in 2027. The initiative seeks to explore the country’s history, from ancient to modern times, through theatrical productions, publications and curated exhibitions. The production is expected to contribute to renewed public engagement with Ghana’s history, particularly among younger generations, by presenting the lives and experiences of historical figures through live performance. The first part of Nkrumah Showboy focuses on the early years of Nkrumah’s life, with a second instalment planned to explore his journey through the independence struggle, presidency, overthrow and exile. Bambu Heritage Productions has built a reputation for bringing African heritage stories to the stage, most notably through Mansa Musa and the Trail of Lost Gold , which has reached audiences in Ghana and internationally. The upcoming preview offers audiences an opportunity to experience the new production as Ghana prepares for the milestone anniversary in 2027. Event details Production: Nkrumah Showboy: Part One: The Boy from Nkroful Date: Friday, 16 October 2026 Time: 7.30 pm Venue: National Theatre, Accra Website: www.nkrumahshowboy.com

items.title: Coastal Highway: Niger Delta groups urge FG to restore original route
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Niger Delta groups have urged the Federal Government to revert to the original alignment of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway to include riverine communities in Ondo, Delta, Bayelsa and other coastal states. The groups, under the aegis of Niger Delta Concerned Stakeholders for Accountable Security and Progress (NDCSASP) and the 21st Century Youths of Niger Delta, condemned the proposed diversion of sections of the highway away from the original coastal route, insisting that Ilaje, Itsekiri and Ijaw communities must not be excluded from the project. They argued that bypassing the communities would undermine the highway’s objective of opening up the coastline to investment, tourism, port development and new coastal cities. In a statement issued on Wednesday and signed by their spokesman, Enisuo Oruomoni, the groups called on President Bola Tinubu to ensure the original master plan was fully implemented. They said the Federal Government should extend to Niger Delta riverine communities the same infrastructure provided along the Lagos section of the highway, including beachfront roads, shore protection and bridges across creeks. “We completely agree with Comrade Tsaye Mene. This is not acceptable if it is true. What is done in Lagos State should be done in other riverine communities and states,” the statement said. The groups were reacting to concerns raised by Mene, convener of Warri Reclamation Thrust and a former national executive member of the Itsekiri National Youths Council, over the reported diversion of the coastal highway from its original alignment. They acknowledged explanations from the Presidency and the Minister of Works, David Umahi, concerning the bypassing of some coastal communities and the proposed realignment towards the East-West Road. However, they appealed to the Federal Government to retain the coastal route, arguing that the project was not merely a transportation corridor but also an opportunity to protect vulnerable communities from coastal erosion and ocean surges. “This road is not just for transportation. It is an environmental protection infrastructure. It will help in protecting and reclaiming the coastlines which oil exploration activities and ocean surge are wiping off daily,” the groups said. They listed Ugborodo, Ogidigben, Ayetoro, Arogbo-Ibe, Gbaramatu, Ekeremor, Ekeni, Ezetu, Furopah, Koloama and Brass among the communities they said were threatened by coastal erosion and needed shore protection. The groups maintained that the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and the East-West Road served different purposes and should not be treated as interchangeable projects. According to them, while the East-West Road provides inland connectivity, the coastal highway is intended to open up underserved coastal areas to economic activities and infrastructure development. “The Coastal Highway and East-West Road are two different projects with different economic objectives. One cannot replace the other,” the statement said. The groups also argued that the original alignment should run from Lagos through Ogun Waterside, Ilaje and Arogbo-Ibe in Ondo State, the coastal communities of Delta and Bayelsa states, and onward through Rivers and Akwa Ibom states to Calabar. They expressed disagreement with the cost-saving argument attributed to Umahi, insisting that Niger Delta communities deserved the same level of engineering investment and infrastructure as other sections of the highway. The groups cited the reported expenditure on a section of the road in Lagos as justification for their demand that comparable infrastructure, including bridges and shoreline protection, be provided in the Niger Delta. They urged Tinubu to intervene and ensure that the original alignment was maintained, arguing that oil-producing communities should benefit from infrastructure funded substantially by the country’s oil wealth. Despite their criticism of the proposed route change, the groups said they remained supporters of Tinubu, expressing confidence that the President would address their concerns. They cited the administration’s policies on electricity decentralisation, local government autonomy, funding for the Niger Delta Development Commission and the Presidential Amnesty Programme, as well as port dredging, among reasons for their continued support. “We remain loyal supporters of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and High Chief Government Ekpemupolo (Tompolo)’s door-to-door campaign for his re-election,” the statement said. The groups warned that excluding Ilaje, Itsekiri and Ijaw coastal communities would defeat the project’s stated objective of opening up the coastline and called for the full implementation of the original master plan. “Our communities must not be bypassed,” they said. items.title: Only youths ignorant of Atiku’s history can be hoodwinked – Keyamo
items.description: By Nwafor Sunday Polycarp Minister of Aviation, Festus Keyamo, SAN, has criticised former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar over his comments on the economic hardship and insecurity in the country, accusing him of hypocrisy and saying only younger Nigerians unfamiliar with his record could be misled by his claims. Keyamo, who made the remarks in a post on his X account on Wednesday, challenged Atiku’s criticism of President Bola Tinubu’s administration, citing the liquidation of Nigeria Airways in September 2004 and the alleged failure to pay the pensions and gratuities of its former workers. The minister argued that the Tinubu administration was addressing the outstanding entitlements of the airline’s former workers, claiming that the President had approved and released N36 billion to provide relief to affected families. According to Keyamo, some of the beneficiaries had begun receiving payment notifications, while the workers’ union had also recognised Tinubu for the intervention. He said it was hypocritical for Atiku to criticise the current administration over hardship without addressing issues arising from decisions taken when he served as vice-president under former President Olusegun Obasanjo. “It’s only the younger ones who don’t know your history you can attempt to hoodwink, but we will expose you to them,” Keyamo wrote. The minister also accused Atiku of taking credit for the achievements of the Obasanjo administration when convenient while distancing himself from its decisions at other times. “When it is convenient for you, you claim some credit of the Obasanjo-Atiku government and when not convenient, you say Obasanjo was in charge and not you as Vice-President,” he said. Keyamo’s comments followed Atiku’s appeal to Nigerians over the rising cost of living and insecurity, in which the former vice-president said families were struggling to afford food, healthcare, transportation and other basic necessities. In his message, Atiku expressed concern about the difficulties confronting pensioners, young workers and parents, as well as the fear experienced by families amid reports of kidnappings and attacks across the country. He said no Nigerian family should have to contend with hunger and insecurity simultaneously, warning against allowing the prevailing conditions to become the future inherited by the next generation. Atiku also urged registered voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), describing them as instruments through which Nigerians could peacefully demand change. “Bola made life expensive. I will work to make life affordable again and restore the security every Nigerian deserves,” he said, calling on citizens across generations to support his vision of a country where families could live with dignity, safety and hope. The exchange comes amid growing political mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections, with political leaders increasingly using public statements and social media to criticise their opponents and promote their policy positions. items.title: Mois du consommer local : Le ministère de l’Économie mobilisé en faveur des produits locaux
items.description: Dans le cadre du Mois du consommer local, le ministère de l’Économie et des Finances organise, du 14 au 16 octobre 2026, une série d’activités visant à promouvoir les produits locaux et à encourager la consommation des productions nationales. Le lancement de ces activités est intervenu dans la matinée du mercredi 14 octobre, en présence de la ministre déléguée chargée du Budget, Fatoumata Bako/Traoré, représentant le ministre de l’Économie et des Finances, Dr Aboubacar Nacanabo, et de la ministre en charge de la Solidarité, le lieutenant-colonel Passowendé Pélagie Kaboré. La cérémonie a été marquée par une montée des couleurs nationales et une remise de vivres et de vêtements au ministère chargé de la Solidarité. C’est en chœur que le personnel du ministère de l’Économie et des Finances a entonné l’hymne national, ce mercredi matin. Aux côtés des deux membres du gouvernement, les agents ont réaffirmé ainsi leur attachement à la patrie et aux valeurs qui fondent le vivre-ensemble au Burkina Faso. Une montée des couleurs a ouvert de lancement à cette activité À l’issue de la montée des couleurs, le ministère a procédé à une remise de dons au département en charge de la Solidarité. Le lot est composé de 3 000 pagnes traditionnels, de 10 tonnes de riz et de 10 tonnes de maïs. Cette initiative vise à apporter un soutien aux actions de solidarité nationale, tout en s’inscrivant dans le programme d’activités du Mois du consommer local. Dans la même dynamique, un espace d’exposition a été aménagé au profit des artisans et des producteurs locaux afin de leur permettre de présenter leurs produits et de valoriser leur savoir-faire. À l’issue de la visite des stands, la ministre déléguée chargée du Budget, Fatoumata Bako/Traoré, a souligné l’importance de la consommation locale dans la valorisation des richesses nationales. La ministre déléguée en charge du budget remettant symboliquement le don à son homologue de la solidarité « Produire est un acte de création, transformer est un acte de valorisation, mais consommer local est un acte qui donne à la production nationale sa raison d’être et son avenir », a-t-elle déclaré. Pour la ministre déléguée, les multiples chocs internationaux, notamment les tensions géopolitiques, les pressions sur les prix de l’énergie et les aléas climatiques, rappellent la nécessité pour les pays de renforcer leur autonomie économique. Selon elle, un pays qui dépend exclusivement de l’extérieur pour satisfaire ses besoins fondamentaux reste vulnérable aux décisions, aux fluctuations des prix et aux événements qu’il ne maîtrise pas toujours. Une vue des stands d'exposition « La souveraineté économique ne signifie pas que nous devons fermer nos portes au monde. Elle signifie que nous devons être capables de choisir nos dépendances, de maîtriser nos priorités et de mobiliser nos propres ressources pour construire notre avenir », a-t-elle indiqué. Cette célébration s’inscrit également dans le cadre de la septième édition du Mois du consommer local dans l’espace de l’Union économique et monétaire ouest-africaine (UEMOA). Placée sous le thème « Consommer local, facteur d’intégration régionale, de solidarité et de souveraineté économique de l’UEMOA face aux mutations du commerce mondial » , cette édition met en avant le rôle de la consommation locale dans le renforcement de l’intégration régionale et de la souveraineté économique. Plus de détails à suivre sur Minute.bf.

items.title: SEC to develop Social Bond Guidelines; over half of listed firms report on ESG indicators
items.description: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is in the process of developing Social Bond Guidelines aligned with the International Capital Market Association’s ICMA Social Bond Principles (SBP). According to the SEC, the guidelines would aim to encourage the development of a credible and transparent social bond market, promote financing for projects that deliver positive social outcomes while ensuring integrity, transparency, and accountability in the issuance and reporting of social bonds. Eligible uses of proceeds will include affordable basic infrastructure, essential services such as healthcare and education, affordable housing, employment and Small and Medium Enterprises support, food security, and the empowerment of vulnerable populations. Overall, the SEC’s approach is explicit about aligning capital market development with national and global sustainability goals. The SEC adopted a structured approach to integrating sustainable finance into the domestic capital market under the Capital Market Master Plan (2020–2029). Its strategy rests on three mutually reinforcing pillars: Standardised Disclosure, Credible Green Finance Instruments, and Strong Governance and Enforcement. These measures aim to enhance transparency, improve disclosure quality, protect investors, reduce greenwashing risks, and mobilise private capital for environmentally and socially beneficial projects. To this end, SEC approved the Ghana Stock Exchange (GSE)’s ESG Disclosure Guidance Manual in 2022, which adopts the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards as the common ESG reporting framework for listed companies. The manual guides materiality, sector-specific disclosures, and the integration of ESG into corporate strategy and reporting. By promoting a single internationally recognised framework, the SEC seeks to improve comparability, strengthen disclosure quality, and boost investor confidence. More than half of the 39 listed companies now report on ESG indicators, reflecting progress while highlighting the need for continued capacity building.

items.title: UBEC: $552m World Bank grant targets 29m Nigerian children, 500,000 teachers
items.description: …13,000 classrooms planned as agency warns states over 2027 budget provisions By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Universal Basic Education Commission, UBEC, has unveiled an ambitious plan to reach 29 million Nigerian children with improved basic education under a $552.18 million World Bank-supported programme, warning state governments that failure to provide the required funding could jeopardise its implementation. The Human Capital Opportunities for Prosperity and Equity in Education (HOPE-EDU) programme is also targeting 500,000 teachers, 65,000 public schools and 10,000 non-formal learning centres nationwide, alongside the construction of 13,000 new classrooms. But the Federal Government’s ambition to expand access to quality education now faces a critical test at the state level, with UBEC insisting that governors must demonstrate the political will and financial commitment required to unlock the programme’s benefits. The Executive Secretary of UBEC, Dr Aisha Garba, raised the concern on Tuesday in Abuja at a two-day meeting with chairmen of State Universal Basic Education Boards (SUBEBs) on implementation readiness. Garba disclosed that the programme became effective on February 27, 2026, and had entered its implementation phase, stressing that states must act swiftly to incorporate relevant activities and funding provisions into their 2027 budgets. According to her, several of the programme’s disbursement-linked indicators depend on states making adequate budgetary allocations, warning that failure to meet the requirements could affect their ability to access the corresponding funds. She said: “A lot of the deliverables for Year 1 will require provisions in the states’ 2027 budget.” The UBEC boss, therefore, directed SUBEB chairmen to take the programme’s implementation report to their respective state executives, secure their commitment and ensure that the necessary financial provisions were made in good time. The warning places state governments at the centre of the initiative, which is designed to improve learning outcomes, reduce inequalities in access to education and strengthen accountability in the delivery of basic education across Nigeria. Garba explained that HOPE-EDU adopts a results-based financing model under which disbursements are tied to the achievement of agreed targets and performance indicators. Under its funding structure, $262.239 million has been earmarked for improving the quality of basic education, $123.9 million for expanding access, while $133.611 million is allocated to strengthening key systems. The three result areas are designed to address persistent challenges in the basic education sector, including poor learning outcomes, inadequate educational access and weaknesses in institutional capacity and accountability. Garba said the quality component would focus on improving teaching standards, providing essential learning resources and raising pupils’ achievement levels in participating states. A key intervention under this component is the adoption of the Structured Pedagogy Programme (SPP), which is intended to strengthen the teaching of literacy and numeracy in primary schools. She said the programme would build on existing Universal Basic Education interventions while complementing other government initiatives in governance and primary healthcare. The UBEC executive secretary disclosed that the programme’s three result areas have different participation requirements. According to her, the first result area, which focuses on improving education quality, is open to 33 states, with participation potentially extending to all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, subject to involvement in the HOPE-GOV operations. The second result area, which targets increased access to education, is designed for 15 states with the highest populations of out-of-school children that also satisfy other eligibility requirements. The third component, focused on strengthening key systems, is open to all 36 states and the FCT. The varying eligibility conditions mean that states must understand the requirements attached to each component and ensure they meet the relevant benchmarks to benefit from the programme. Garba said successful implementation would require close coordination among state ministries of education, SUBEBs, Local Education Authorities, schools and School-Based Management Committees. She urged SUBEB chairmen, whom she described as key drivers of basic education implementation at the state level, to take ownership of the programme and ensure that their states meet the agreed targets and verification requirements. Garba said the initiative, introduced under President Bola Tinubu’s administration, was intended to ensure that every Nigerian child, particularly those in rural communities, marginalised populations and out-of-school groups, had equitable opportunities to access quality education. However, she emphasised that achieving this objective would depend on translating policy commitments into concrete action, particularly through adequate budgetary provisions and effective coordination at the state level. “The success of HOPE-EDU rests on your shoulders. Let us work together to ensure that no state is left behind,” she told the SUBEB chairmen. She urged participants to engage actively during the meeting, seek clarification on implementation requirements and return to their respective states as advocates for the programme. Garba also commended the National Programme Coordinator, the Programme Manager and the HOPE-EDU team for organising the meeting, while acknowledging the support of the Federal Ministry of Education, the World Bank and other technical partners. Earlier, the Programme Manager of HOPE-EDU, Mr Olumayowa Aleshin, presented an overview of the initiative, outlining its funding arrangements, implementation targets and key milestones. The programme’s framework requires participating states to meet specified performance targets and verification requirements before qualifying for the corresponding disbursements. With 29 million children, 500,000 teachers, thousands of schools and non-formal learning centres covered by its targets, HOPE-EDU represents a major intervention in Nigeria’s basic education sector. Its ultimate impact, however, will depend on whether federal and state authorities can convert the funding commitments into classrooms, better teaching, improved learning outcomes and wider access to education for millions of children. items.title: Insurance firms have up till January 2027 to incorporate ESG in financial reporting
items.description: Beginning January 2027, all insurance companies will have to incorporate Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) in their financial reporting or face sanctions. This follows the integration of ESG principles within the insurance industry in 2023 by the National Insurance Commission (NIC). In partnership with the German Development Agency for International Cooperation (GIZ) and Financial Sector Deepening (FSD) Africa, the NIC conducted a comprehensive diagnostic study to evaluate ESG integration across the sector, aimed at identifying key gaps, opportunities, and areas for further advancement. It then set a voluntary deadline for January 2026. The move is part of Sustainable Finance Roadmap led by the Bank of Ghana and with support from the other financial regulators. The NIC initiated its integration of ESG principles within the insurance industry in 2023. A targeted survey was implemented to collect data from industry stakeholders. This allowed the NIC to assess the market’s adoption of ESG principles and ESG-related risks and opportunities, as well as to gauge the extent of ESG integration within company operations. Based on the survey findings, the NIC developed and issued an industry guideline in December 2024, outlining general and specific requirements for regulated entities on ESG integration across the insurance value chain. To facilitate industry compliance with these guidelines, the NIC introduced a suite of toolkits designed for self-assessment. These resources enable insurers to evaluate their current position regarding ESG and lay the groundwork for establishing a comprehensive Roadmap. Subsequently, the NIC undertook several capacity-building initiatives addressing persons in charge of governance on the relevance of institutionalising ESG principles across their operations. Other training sessions were delivered to the senior management and persons designated as ESG-responsible officers across the sector. The training emphasised the importance of integrating ESG into core business processes, highlighting that such integration extends beyond regulatory compliance and represents a strategic step towards long-term sustainability.

items.title: Saison des pluies à Dakar : la galère des conducteurs de motos-taxis
items.description: La saison des pluies est une période éprouvante pour les Dakarois. À chaque coin de rue, la pluie laisse derrière elle d'imposantes flaques d’eau et de nombreux secteurs d'activité en pâtissent. Les motocyclistes ne sont pas épargnés. Entre les averses battantes et les inondations, les « Jakartamen » de la capitale doivent redoubler d'efforts pour joindre les deux bouts. Ils sont juste à côté de l’entrée principale de l’Université Cheikh Anta Diop (Ucad) de Dakar, sur l’avenue du même nom. Ils ont tous un point commun : ce sont des conducteurs de motos-taxis. Assis à l’ombre d’un arbre pour fuir les dards torrides de ce début d'après-midi du 23 septembre 2026, ce groupe de jeunes hommes guette tout potentiel client. La saison des pluies ne semble pas être une bonne période pour eux, les conditions de travail n’étant pas réunies. Pour Assane Dieng, qui se distingue comme étant le benjamin du groupe, il n’est pas question de conduire sous les averses. En débardeur, hésitant au début, il finit par lâcher : « Je ne compte pas rouler quand il pleut, je ne le ferai jamais. Je préfère attendre que la pluie s’estompe ». Il en est de même pour Mohamed Ngom, assis à même le sol, un mouchoir sur la tête pour se protéger de la chaleur. Étudiant en Master 2 au département de portugais de la Faculté des lettres et sciences humaines de l’Ucad, il fait ce job pendant les vacances. Les arguments qu’il donne sont plutôt techniques. « Quand il pleut, il vaut mieux éviter de conduire, car l’eau peut endommager le moteur. De plus, la pluie réduit fortement la visibilité, ce qui constitue le principal danger », explique-t-il, mimant la scène de la main. « Si ta vision devient floue en cours de route, tu peux à tout moment entrer en collision avec un bus ou tomber dans un trou. C'est trop dangereux », assène le « Jakartaman ». Pour Mohamed et Assane, la consigne est claire : attendre l'éclaircie. « C’est plus prudent », concluent-ils. Ainsi, pour ces conducteurs, enfourcher la moto dans cette masse d’eau relève de la mission impossible. Tel n’est pas le cas de leur collègue Thiéffi Fall. Teint noir, physiquement élancé, il ne voit aucun inconvénient à braver les intempéries. « Je roule sous la pluie sans problème. Je suis obligé de le faire ; si un client arrive, je ne vais pas le refuser juste parce qu’il pleut », déclare-t-il, sourire aux lèvres. Si certains de ses confrères prévoient des imperméables pour leurs passagers et pour eux-mêmes, ce n’est pas son cas. « Je n’ai pas d’imperméable et je ne pense pas en acheter », tranche-t-il. Du côté des clients, l'engouement pour les motos « Jakarta » ne faiblit pas, surtout à l'heure de rentrer. Beaucoup ne voient aucun inconvénient à monter sur deux roues, avec ou sans imperméable. La haute saison des mécanos L’essentiel pour eux est d’arriver à destination le plus vite possible. Ablaye Sy a l’air pressé. Ce jeune homme de taille moyenne est un habitué des motos-taxis. Déjà installé derrière son conducteur, il confie : « Je suis un adepte des motos Jakarta parce que c’est plus rapide. Cependant, lorsqu'il pleut, je préfère prendre un taxi pour me rendre dans un endroit important comme le bureau, histoire de rester présentable ». Mais il s’empresse de préciser que « s'il s'agit juste de rentrer à la maison, aucun problème, je prends la moto ». Pape Ndiaye, un autre client, ne prend jamais de moto « Jakarta » quand il pleut ou quand il a fini de pleuvoir ; il y va de sa propre sécurité : « Quand il a fini de pleuvoir, les voies sont glissantes et beaucoup de motocyclistes sont victimes d’accidents durant cette période. Je ne compte donc pas prendre un tel risque juste après ou pendant qu’il pleut », soutient-il, casque sur la tête, prêt à monter derrière le motocycliste. Henry, assis avec deux autres de ses compagnons à l’ombre, rappelle qu’il ne prend le « Thiak-Thiak » qu’en cas d’urgence. « Si je suis vraiment pressé, je peux prendre la moto ; cependant, je préfère attendre que la pluie s’estompe par mesure de prudence », confie-t-il. Son ami Oumar embouche la même trompette, tandis que Mor Diaw, assis au milieu des deux, jure n’avoir jamais pris de « Thiak-Thiak » : « Je ne suis jamais monté sur une moto et je ne compte pas le faire. Je n’ai pas confiance aux motocyclistes, ils conduisent comme ils veulent et c’est dangereux, surtout lorsqu’il pleut ». L’eau de pluie reste le pire ennemi des deux-roues. Lorsqu’elle s’infiltre dans le système électrique, elle provoque fréquemment des courts-circuits et noie les moteurs. Installé dans son garage du Point E, Souleymane Diallo répare des motos depuis maintenant quatre ans. Il témoigne : « Pendant l'hivernage, le travail double. L'eau entre dans les carburateurs, mouille les bougies ou crée des masses électriques. On passe nos journées à dépanner des Jakartamen tombés en panne au milieu des flaques. C'est dur pour eux, mais pour nous, les mécaniciens, c'est la haute saison ! » Irène MENDY (Stagiaire)

items.title: Éducation : les enseignants contractuels de Conakry dénoncent une « trahison » syndicale et appellent à quitter les classes
items.description: Les enseignants contractuels de la zone spéciale de Conakry sont montés au créneau ce mercredi 14 octobre 2026. Réunis devant la Bourse du travail, à Kaloum, ils ont dénoncé ce qu’ils qualifient de « trahison » de la part de l’intersyndicale de l’éducation et exigé l’application du protocole d’accord signé avec le gouvernement le 3 janvier 2026. Ils appellent leurs collègues à quitter les salles de classe jusqu’à la satisfaction de leurs revendications. S’exprimant au nom du mouvement, Latise Ibrahim Salim, coordinateur général des enseignants contractuels de la zone spéciale de Conakry, a exprimé sa déception face à la gestion de leur dossier par les organisations syndicales. « Chers camarades, chers combattants des luttes, c’est avec un cœur rempli de déception que la coordination des enseignants contractuels de la zone spéciale de Conakry s’adresse aujourd’hui à la nation mondiale, à la suite de la trahison de l’intersyndicale de l’éducation vis-à-vis de notre situation et du non-respect du protocole d’accord signé le 3 janvier 2026 entre l’intersyndicale de l’éducation, la FSPE, le SNE et le SLECG. Aujourd’hui, au nom de la coordination des enseignants contractuels de la zone spéciale de Conakry, nous informons l’opinion nationale et internationale de l’état d’avancement de notre dossier », a-t-il déclaré. Selon le coordinateur général, leur dossier serait désormais relégué au second plan. « À date, nous informons tous les enseignants contractuels de la zone spéciale de Conakry que le dossier est déjà oublié à la suite de la trahison de l’intersyndicale de l’éducation vis-à-vis du gouvernement. La coordination exige, sans délai, le respect du protocole d’accord signé le 3 janvier 2026 », a-t-il affirmé. Dans la foulée, Latise Ibrahim Salim a appelé ses collègues exerçant dans les établissements publics à suspendre les cours jusqu’à la satisfaction de leurs revendications. « Nous demandons à tous les enseignants contractuels de la zone spéciale de Conakry de quitter les salles de classe au niveau des établissements publics jusqu’à la satisfaction de notre revendication, qui n’est rien d’autre que l’application du protocole d’accord du 3 janvier 2026 et l’intégration des enseignants contractuels de la zone spéciale de Conakry à la fonction publique, en passant par le concours pratique de classe. Parce qu’on ne peut connaître la valeur d’un enseignant que dans sa classe », a-t-il soutenu. Le porte-parole a également interpellé le président de la République, le général Mamadi Doumbouya, ainsi que le Premier ministre, Amadou Oury Bah, les exhortant à s’impliquer personnellement pour trouver une issue à ce dossier qui, selon lui, traîne depuis 2018. « Nous sommes dans cette situation et celle des anciens contractuels communautaires a déjà évolué. Il ne faudrait pas que nous soyons les oubliés de la zone spéciale de Conakry. […] L’État a demandé 8 000. Il y a un besoin de 8 000 pour le moment. Mais le besoin général, au lancement, était de 18 000. De nos jours, l’État dit qu’il ne peut engager que 8 000. Et Conakry, qui n’atteint même pas 2 000, pourquoi ne pas les évaluer en classe ou, à défaut, les engager sans condition ? », a-t-il plaidé. Les enseignants contractuels de la zone spéciale de Conakry réclament ainsi une réponse des autorités et l’application des engagements pris dans le cadre du protocole d’accord du 3 janvier 2026. items.title: Loi de finances 2027 : Entre contraintes constitutionnelles et promesses électorales
items.description: Alors que le projet de loi de finances pour 2027 doit être déposé au Parlement au plus tard le 20 octobre, la formation d’une nouvelle majorité autour de Fatima Zahra El Mansouri intervient dans un calendrier particulièrement contraint. Si le texte budgétaire repose sur des hypothèses économiques déjà définies, le futur exécutif conserve la possibilité de le modifier, y compris après son adoption, selon un spécialiste des finances publiques. Le temps politique et le calendrier budgétaire avancent à des rythmes différents. Au Maroc, le projet de loi de finances pour l’exercice 2027 entre dans sa dernière semaine avant la date limite de son dépôt à la Chambre des représentants, fixée au 20 octobre par la loi organique relative à la loi de finances. Dans le même temps, les tractations s’accélèrent en vue de la formation d’un nouveau gouvernement, qui doit être dirigé par Fatima Zahra El Mansouri, après l’annonce d’une alliance quadripartite réunissant le Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM), le Parti de l’Istiqlal, l’Union socialiste des forces populaires (USFP) et le Parti du progrès et du socialisme (PPS). Dans un communiqué publié lundi 12 octobre, les quatre formations ont indiqué qu’elles « proposeront des noms de ministres et de ministres répondant aux critères de compétence, de sens politique, d’intégrité et de probité ». Elles affichent l’ambition de constituer un gouvernement « cohérent et fort », en mesure de « mettre en œuvre un programme gouvernemental qui sera élaboré dans les plus brefs délais ». Mais la constitution de cette équipe ne saurait suspendre les obligations du calendrier institutionnel. D’ici au mardi 20 octobre, le projet de loi de finances doit avoir été officiellement transmis au Parlement, indépendamment de l’avancement des négociations politiques. Un calendrier budgétaire encadré par la loi organique La contrainte est d’abord juridique. L’article 48 de la loi organique n° 130.13 relative à la loi de finances dispose que le projet de loi de finances de l’année suivante doit être déposé, en priorité, au bureau de la Chambre des représentants au plus tard le 20 octobre de l’exercice en cours. Le dossier doit être accompagné de treize documents, parmi lesquels figurent la note de présentation, le rapport économique et financier ainsi que plusieurs rapports thématiques. L’article 46 confie la préparation du projet au ministre chargé des finances, sous l’autorité du chef du gouvernement. L’élaboration du texte doit tenir compte des orientations générales examinées en Conseil des ministres, conformément à l’article 49 de la Constitution de 2011. Une fois déposé, le projet suit un parcours parlementaire dont les délais sont également définis par la loi organique. L’article 49 accorde trente jours à la Chambre des représentants pour examiner le texte, puis vingt-deux jours à la Chambre des conseillers. Le projet retourne ensuite à la première chambre pour une seconde lecture, définitive, dans un délai de six jours. L’hypothèse d’une adoption tardive est elle aussi prévue par les textes. Si le Parlement ne parvient pas à voter le budget avant le 31 décembre, l’article 50 autorise le gouvernement à ouvrir, par décret, les crédits nécessaires au fonctionnement des services publics. Le recouvrement des recettes se poursuit alors selon les dispositions en vigueur. Le précédent de 2021 illustre la proximité entre la formation d’une majorité et la préparation du budget. Le gouvernement d’Aziz Akhannouch avait déposé le projet de loi de finances pour 2022 le 18 octobre de cette année-là, quelques semaines après les élections. Le texte avait intégré des dispositions correspondant aux engagements électoraux de la nouvelle équipe. Des prévisions économiques confrontées aux incertitudes internationales Au-delà des délais, les hypothèses économiques retenues pour 2027 constituent un autre enjeu pour le prochain exécutif. La note d’orientation prévoit une croissance de 4,1 %, une inflation proche de 2 % et une récolte céréalière de 70 millions de quintaux. Elle retient également un prix du pétrole de 70 dollars le baril et un cours du gaz butane de 500 dollars la tonne. Selon les données publiées, la croissance attendue devrait reposer principalement sur le dynamisme des activités non agricoles, sans mobilisation de recettes exceptionnelles. Ces prévisions se heurtent toutefois à un environnement international incertain. Au début d’octobre 2026, les contrats à terme sur le pétrole brut Brent se maintenaient au-dessus de 100 dollars le baril, soit un niveau sensiblement supérieur à celui retenu dans les hypothèses budgétaires. Lors de sa présentation devant les deux commissions des finances, la ministre de l’économie et des finances avait elle-même souligné les incertitudes liées aux tensions géopolitiques au Moyen-Orient et à leurs répercussions sur les prix de l’énergie et les chaînes d’approvisionnement. La loi organique encadre également la manière dont ces prévisions doivent être établies. Son article 10 impose aux lois de finances de présenter sincèrement l’ensemble des ressources et des charges. Cette exigence est appréciée au regard des informations disponibles au moment de l’élaboration du projet. L’article 9 prévoit, quant à lui, que le solde budgétaire prévisionnel est évalué à partir des hypothèses ayant servi à construire le texte. Le futur gouvernement peut-il modifier le projet ? L’arrivée d’une nouvelle équipe gouvernementale soulève dès lors une question : dans quelle mesure pourra-t-elle faire évoluer un projet préparé par le gouvernement sortant ? Interpelé par Hespress , Jaouad Laassri, professeur de l’enseignement supérieur à la faculté des sciences juridiques, économiques et sociales de Mohammedia et spécialiste de la législation financière et des finances publiques, met en garde contre une « confusion fréquente » au sujet de la nature juridique des lois organiques, y compris chez certains universitaires et enseignants-chercheurs. Il rappelle que la loi organique relative aux finances publiques « fait partie intégrante du texte constitutionnel, dans la mesure où les lois organiques n’entrent en vigueur et ne deviennent applicables qu’après que la Cour constitutionnelle a confirmé leur conformité à la Constitution ». Dès lors, toute atteinte à ses dispositions ou toute violation de celles-ci constitue, selon lui, « une violation explicite de la Constitution elle-même ». Cette exigence juridique ne signifie cependant pas que le projet de loi de finances serait intangible. Jaouad Laassri estime que le gouvernement dispose de toutes les prérogatives nécessaires pour en modifier le contenu. Les changements peuvent être introduits avant le dépôt officiel du texte, prévu au plus tard le 20 octobre, à l’initiative du gouvernement lui-même. Ils peuvent également intervenir pendant l’examen parlementaire, à travers des propositions présentées par les partis de la majorité et acceptées par l’exécutif. Le spécialiste considère cette possibilité comme une issue politique appropriée, permettant de prendre en compte les orientations de la nouvelle majorité sans remettre en cause le cadre constitutionnel. La marge de manœuvre ne disparaît pas non plus après l’adoption du budget. « Même dans le scénario où la loi serait promulguée en 2027, rien ne s’oppose à la modification ultérieure de ses dispositions au moyen de lois de finances rectificatives », explique Jaouad Laassri, qui souligne que « toutes les options et possibilités constitutionnelles demeurent ouvertes ». Le professeur réitère ainsi que le gouvernement peut modifier le projet avant son dépôt ou pendant son examen parlementaire, si les propositions des partis de la majorité sont acceptées. Le recours à des lois de finances rectificatives demeure également possible après la promulgation de la loi. Des engagements électoraux à traduire dans le budget Cette latitude prend une importance particulière au regard des promesses formulées pendant la campagne électorale. Le Parti authenticité et modernité, qui a remporté 97 sièges sur les 395 que compte la Chambre des représentants, avait présenté un programme dont le coût supplémentaire annoncé atteignait 350 milliards de dirhams sur la période 2027-2031. L’ampleur de cet engagement pose la question de sa traduction budgétaire, alors que les premières hypothèses de la loi de finances ont été définies avant la mise en place du nouvel exécutif. Dans ce contexte, plusieurs analyses privilégient le scénario d’une modification partielle du projet plutôt que celui d’une réécriture intégrale du budget de l’année prochaine. La note d’orientation publiée le 5 août 2026 par Aziz Akhannouch, chef du gouvernement sortant, constitue le cadre initial de cette préparation. Elle appelait les différents départements ministériels à « rationaliser les dépenses et à limiter la création de nouveaux postes budgétaires aux besoins indispensables ». Le document retenait quatre priorités : consolider les acquis économiques, réduire les disparités territoriales et sociales, poursuivre la consolidation des fondements de l’État social et préserver les équilibres des finances publiques. Pour autant, ces orientations ne lient pas nécessairement le prochain gouvernement sur le plan politique. Abderrazak El Hiri, professeur de finances et d’économie à l’université Sidi Mohamed Ben Abdellah de Fès, estimait que « la note n’a de caractère contraignant sur le plan administratif qu’au stade de la préparation ». Dans une précédente déclaration à Hespress , il avait précisé que le document « ne lie pas politiquement le prochain gouvernement au sens absolu du terme ». The post Loi de finances 2027 : Entre contraintes constitutionnelles et promesses électorales appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Burkina/Nécrologie: El hadj Aboubacar Tiemtoré dit « Ladji 14 » repose éternellement à Nomgana
items.description: El Hadj Aboubacar Tiemtoré plus connu sous le pseudonyme « Ladji 14 », une figure emblématique du cyclisme burkinabè, décédé, le mardi 14 octobre 2026, des suites de maladie, repose désormais éternellement dans le village Nomgana, sur la route de Ziniaré, dans le centre du Burkina Faso. L’information était tombée comme un couperet pour le monde sportif notamment ceux de la discipline cyclisme, le mardi 13 octobre 2026, suite à l’annonce du décès de « Ladji 14 » de son nom à l’état-civil, El hadj Aboubacar Tiemtoré. En effet, l’ancien cycliste et promoteur d’activité sportive notamment le cyclisme, El hadj Aboubacar Tiemtoré, célèbre animateur de radio, s’est éteint et a déposé définitivement le micro, plongeant ses fans dans un choc indescriptible. On le savait diminué par la maladie. Ladji 14 a définitivement déposé le micro « Ancien coureur, animateur chevronné et promoteur, il était un grand passionné du cyclisme burkinabè, auquel il a consacré une très grande partie de sa vie. Sa disparition, à quelques jours du Tour du Faso 2026, constitue une grande perte pour le monde du cyclisme national », a écrit la Fédération nationale de cyclisme dans un communiqué. Celui que les Burkinabè appelaient affectueusement « Ladji 14 » a été accompagné à sa dernière demeure à Nomgana, son village natal situé sur la route de Ziniaré, capitale de la région d’Oubri dans le centre du pays. Pour reconnaître l’apport immense de « Ladji 14 », un Grand Prix dénommé 14 avait été institué pour l’honorer et encourager la jeune génération de cycliste. El hadj 14 fait partie des premiers cycliste aux premières heures du célèbre Tour du Faso dont la 37 e édition aura lieu dans moins de trois semaines. Grâce à sa passion pour la Petite reine, il avait fini par devenir l'un des animateurs emblématiques, précisément en langue mooré, de ce même Tour et des autres rendez-vous. Par Bernard BOUGOUM L’article Burkina/Nécrologie: El hadj Aboubacar Tiemtoré dit « Ladji 14 » repose éternellement à Nomgana est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Indonesia seeks Nigerian investors, eyes stronger trade ties
items.description: By Favour Ulebor, Jakarta Indonesia is seeking increased investment from Nigerian businesses and stronger bilateral cooperation in renewable energy, waste management, manufacturing and agriculture, while expressing willingness to invest in Nigeria, and expand trade, industrial partnerships between both countries. Speaking to Nigerian journalists ahead of the 41st Trade Expo Indonesia on Tuesday in Jakarta, Senior Trade Analyst at Indonesia’s Ministry of Trade, Iska Huberta Sinural, said bilateral trade should go beyond Nigeria importing Indonesian products to include Nigerian exports, investments and business partnerships in Indonesia. Sinural said the country was targeting $17.5 billion in transactions at the exhibition, which would bring together more than 600 exhibitors to showcase products and explore business opportunities with international buyers and investors. She said Indonesia was particularly interested in attracting buyers from Africa and expanding its business networks beyond traditional markets, while encouraging Nigerian investors to explore opportunities in the Indonesian economy. The analyst said Nigeria had remained among the leading countries in terms of buyers attending the Indonesian trade exhibition, ranking third in 2024 and fourth in 2025, according to figures she presented during the interview. Sinural said the two countries could achieve more through stronger government engagement, noting that trade agreements needed to translate into practical business transactions and investment commitments. She explained that Indonesia wanted officials from partner countries to deepen communication and hold more meetings to implement existing agreements. Sinural said attracting buyers had become increasingly challenging because of geopolitical tensions, global economic conditions and the financial demands on exhibitors. She added that the organisers were focusing on sectors with export potential and seeking reliable exhibitors capable of meeting buyers’ requirements. According to her, the exhibition will feature five broad areas, including food, beverages and agricultural products; manufactured goods; industrial estates and services; fashion and handicrafts; and furniture and home decoration. Also speaking, a member of the Export Enhancement Division of the Indonesian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Muhammad Alpvy, said there were significant untapped opportunities for trade and investment between Indonesia and African countries, including Nigeria. Alpvy said Indonesian businesses were interested in expanding cooperation beyond existing commodity transactions to include manufacturing, renewable energy, waste management and the establishment of factories in Nigeria and Indonesia. He identified palm oil, rubber products, food ingredients and healthcare manufacturing as areas with opportunities for expanded trade, adding that both countries could also explore ways to process raw materials into finished products. Alpvy said high shipping costs and trade barriers remained major challenges to trade between Nigeria and Indonesia, noting that the distance between the two countries increased transportation expenses. He called for further discussions on trade arrangements that would reduce these costs and make it easier for businesses to establish long-term commercial relationships. On investment, Alpvy said Nigerian businesses had expressed interest in renewable energy and waste management, including partnerships that could support the establishment of production facilities. He explained that businesses needed clear arrangements on investment structures, tariffs, shipping costs and other operating conditions to make cross-border investments sustainable. Alpvy also urged Nigerian businesses to introduce local food and beverages to Indonesian consumers, saying greater awareness of Nigerian products and culture could open new markets for both countries. He said Nigerian businesses could adapt their products to Indonesian tastes and consumer preferences, while exploring opportunities to establish Nigerian restaurants and introduce local food products to the market. Alpvy further highlighted opportunities in renewable energy and waste management, including the production of alternative fuel from agricultural and animal waste. He said stronger cooperation in these sectors could create long-term benefits beyond immediate import and export transactions. Separately, Head of International Trade Division at the Regional Office of Industry and Trade of West Java Province, Moch. Lukmanul Hakim, presented data showing growth in the province’s exports to countries within the jurisdiction of the Indonesian Embassy in Abuja, with Nigeria accounting for the largest share of exports recorded during the first eight months of 2026. According to the presentation, West Java’s total exports to the eight countries covered by the Abuja office rose from $275.78 million in 2024 to $383.61 million in 2025. The data further showed that exports to the eight countries amounted to $160.17 million between January and August 2026, of which Nigeria accounted for $109.36 million, representing 68.28 per cent of the total. Other destinations included Ghana, which accounted for $21.85 million, Benin with $9.59 million, Liberia with $3.48 million, Niger with $2.94 million, Togo with $14.96 million and Burkina Faso with $930,000. The presentation also highlighted West Java’s major export commodities, including processed food products, motor vehicles and parts, paper and paperboard, electrical equipment, pharmaceutical products, vegetable oils, beverages and machinery. The figures underscored Nigeria’s importance as a destination for West Java’s exports and the scope for both countries to explore further trade and investment opportunities. The presentation also identified potential Nigerian products for export to Indonesia, including cocoa beans, soybean oilcake, soya beans, sesame seeds, cashew nuts, groundnuts, cotton, cocoa paste, aluminium alloys, lead, rubber-related products and glass containers. Other products highlighted on the export potential map included electrical energy, insecticides, leather products, ethylene polymers and waste and scrap aluminium, pointing to opportunities for Nigeria to diversify its exports to Indonesia beyond crude oil. The Indonesian side also identified challenges associated with Nigeria’s banking system, particularly the difficulties foreign investors may encounter when seeking to open bank accounts to facilitate business transactions. The officials expressed hope that the Nigerian government would look into the concerns to make it easier for foreign businesses to establish operations and sustain commercial relationships in the country. The 41st Trade Expo Indonesia is scheduled to hold from October 14 to 18, 2026, bringing together exporters, buyers, manufacturers and investors to explore trade and investment opportunities. The post Indonesia seeks Nigerian investors, eyes stronger trade ties appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: High Court throws out Afenyo-Markin’s GH¢15m defamation suit against Sammy Gyamfi
items.description: The High Court’s General Jurisdiction 1 has thrown out Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin’s GH¢15 million defamation suit against Ghana Gold Board Chief Executive Officer, Sammy Gyamfi. The court found the writ incurably defective and incompetent, ruling that it could not properly invoke the court’s jurisdiction. In reaching its decision, the court relied on Coleman v Newmont on the applicable procedural rule and Owusu Domena on the requirement to raise objections promptly. The ruling ends the proceedings under the defective writ. It concerns the procedural validity of the action rather than a determination of whether the statements complained of were defamatory. Mr Afenyo-Markin announced the legal action in Parliament on 24 August 2026, saying it followed allegations of extortion made against him amid a dispute over GoldBod and the Bank of Ghana’s Domestic Gold Purchase Programme. The High Court suit also named Multimedia Group Limited as a defendant. The Minority Leader maintained that the allegations were false and intended to damage his reputation. The case subsequently generated disagreement over service of the writ. Mr Gyamfi authorised his lawyers, Ayine & Partners, to accept the court documents, while Mr Afenyo-Markin’s lawyers later said service had been completed and rejected claims that their client was avoiding it.

items.title: Rollover cost of T-bills reduced substantially, one-year bill yield drops 19% since December 2024
items.description: The cost of rolling over Ghana’s local currency debt has substantially reduced since December 2024. Interest rates on Ghana’s six-month treasury bill (182-day bill) have fallen to about 6.5%, and its one-year bill to 10.1% at the end of August 2026, from almost 30% at the end of 2024, S&P Global stated. The Ministry of Finance imposed a three-year ban on the issuance of new medium- or long-term domestic bonds following the domestic debt restructuring in December 2022. In 2026, the government started to issue longer tenor bonds, which should help lengthen the maturity profile of Ghana’s local currency debt. However, S&P said the conflict in the Middle East is likely to erode some of these gains by causing inflation and financing costs to rise and increasing pressure on the cedi. Last week, the government increased its T-bills uptake reflecting higher financing needs following weeks of below-target acceptances. This week’s higher issuance target of GH¢5.02 billion further reinforces this view. However, the GH¢1.53bn raised above last week’s target could temporarily ease funding pressures. Against this backdrop, analyst expect yields to remain broadly stable, as elevated financing needs limit the scope for further declines. This week’s issuance will cover maturing bills of GH¢3.91 billion.

items.title: L’Équipe salue les qualités techniques et tactiques du jeune Abdellah Ouazane
items.description: Le jeune milieu marocain Abdellah Ouazane, nouvelle sensation de l’Ajax Amsterdam, est déjà en avance sur son temps et suscite, à 17 ans seulement, de grandes attentes dans son pays, écrit mercredi le quotidien sportif français « L’Équipe ». La publication spécialisée consacre au jeune prodige un portrait intitulé « Abdellah Ouazane, la nouvelle pépite du Maroc », dans lequel elle revient notamment sur ses débuts avec la sélection marocaine, son parcours en club et les espoirs placés en lui en vue des prochaines échéances internationales. Né à Amsterdam en janvier 2009, Ouazane a choisi de représenter le pays de ses parents, après avoir évolué dans les sélections de jeunes des Pays-Bas et du Maroc, poursuit le quotidien, rappelant que le joueur s’était distingué lors de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations 2025 des moins de 17 ans, organisée au Maroc, où il avait été élu meilleur joueur du tournoi, avec à la clé le titre continental avec la sélection marocaine remporté après sa victoire en finale contre le Mali aux tirs au but (0-0, 4-2). Lancé par le sélectionneur Mohamed Ouahbi, Ouazane a effectué ses débuts avec les Lions de l’Atlas le 25 septembre dernier à Rabat, lors de la victoire contre le Gabon (2-0), devenant le deuxième plus jeune joueur à porter le maillot marocain lors d’un match officiel, derrière l'ancien espoir de l’AC Milan, Hachim Mastour, qui avait débuté à 16 ans en 2015 contre la Libye, fait savoir la publication. En club, le joueur avait été surclassé chez les moins de 19 ans de l’Ajax au cours de la saison 2024-2025. Alors qu’un engagement avec le Real Madrid était envisagé en fin de saison, le club néerlandais l’a intégré à son équipe première à l’été 2026, sous la direction de l’entraîneur espagnol Michel (Miguel Ángel Sánchez Muñoz), indique l'auteur de l'article. Ouazane s’est illustré dès sa première apparition officielle avec l’équipe première de l’Ajax en Championnat des Pays-Bas, le 16 août, en inscrivant un but d’une frappe enroulée dans la lucarne depuis l’extérieur de la surface, après une récupération haute. Le journal relève que le jeune milieu a également été utilisé sur les ailes, une position qui lui permet de travailler sa vitesse, ses replis défensifs et sa polyvalence, mais il est plus à l’aise dans l’axe, aux postes de milieu relayeur ou offensif. Nabil Baha, son ancien sélectionneur chez les moins de 17 ans, cité par « L’Équipe », met en avant ses qualités techniques et tactiques, estimant qu’il « possède un QI footballistique très élevé par rapport à son âge ». Le quotidien souligne enfin que Ouazane anime l’ambition de participer à la Coupe du monde 2030, que le Maroc coorganisera avec le Portugal et l’Espagne. The post L’Équipe salue les qualités techniques et tactiques du jeune Abdellah Ouazane appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .
