items.title: Égypte : une ligne ferroviaire à grande vitesse pour contourner les blocages du canal de Suez
items.description: Le canal de Suez, par lequel transite environ 12 % du commerce maritime mondial, constitue depuis plus d'un siecle un axe strategique pour l'economie egyptienne. Mais les perturbations securitaires en mer Rouge ont mis en evidence la vulnerabilite de cette voie commerciale, contraignant certains navires a contourner l'Afrique par le cap de Bonne-Esperance et affectant les recettes de transit du pays. Pour reduire sa dependance a cette route maritime, Le Caire mise sur le developpement de son reseau ferroviaire. Au cœur de cette strategie figure un reseau electrifie a grande vitesse de 2 000 kilometres, dont le contrat avec Siemens atteint 8,7 milliards de dollars. Presente comme un « canal de Suez sur rails », le projet doit relier les ports de la mer Rouge aux terminaux d'exportation de la Mediterranee. Une fois pleinement operationnelle, l'infrastructure devrait transporter jusqu'a 13 millions de tonnes de marchandises par an. Elle permettra d'acheminer des cargaisons a travers le territoire egyptien et d'offrir un relais au transport maritime, notamment en cas d'interruption des routes commerciales. Le ministre egyptien de la Planification et du Developpement economique Ahmed Rostom a souligne les investissements realises dans les routes, les ports et les chemins de fer pour offrir davantage d'options aux partenaires commerciaux du pays. Les marchandises pourront ainsi transiter par le canal ou emprunter le reseau terrestre pour rejoindre la Mediterranee et acceder aux marches europeens, a-t-il explique. La zone economique du canal au centre du dispositif Le projet s'inscrit dans une strategie logistique plus large, articulee autour de la zone economique du canal de Suez, qui aurait attire pres de 16 milliards de dollars d'investissements. Les autorites egyptiennes entendent egalement developper des plateformes logistiques en partenariat avec le secteur prive afin de faciliter le stockage, le transfert et la distribution des marchandises. Au-dela de la securisation des echanges, Le Caire presente ces infrastructures comme un levier potentiel d'integration commerciale sur le continent. Dans le cadre de la Zone de libre-echange continentale africaine (ZLECAf), les liaisons terrestres pourraient contribuer a connecter les ports nord-africains a des corridors commerciaux desservant l'Afrique de l'Est et l'Afrique subsaharienne. L'objectif affiche est de renforcer la capacite de l'egypte a relier les marches africains, mediterraneens et europeens. Le reseau ferroviaire ne remplace toutefois pas le canal de Suez : il constitue une voie terrestre complementaire destinee a diversifier les itineraires de transport et a limiter les consequences d'eventuelles perturbations maritimes.

items.title: Última hora de la actualidad política, en directo | El PSOE aumenta la distancia sobre el PP hasta los 11,8 puntos tras la convocatoria electoral, según el CIS
items.description: El PSOE sube tres puntos en intención de voto y aumenta su distancia sobre el PP hasta los 11,8 puntos, según el barómetro de octubre del Centro de Investigaciones Sociológicas (CIS), publicado este miércoles. El instituto dirigido por José Félix Tezanos da a los socialistas el 34% de los sufragios, frente al 22,2% que reciben los populares, 3,3 puntos menos que en el estudio anterior. La tercera fuerza del Parlamento en intención de voto es el partido de Santiago Abascal, que suma medio punto respecto a septiembre. Los partidos de Sumar y Frente Amplio reciben un 6,1% de los apoyos y Podemos pierde seis décimas, quedándose en el 3,1%. Mientras, la candidata de Frente Amplio a la presidencia del Gobierno, Ada Colau, ha abierto la puerta a renunciar a encabezar la coalición e incluso a cambiar su nombre para facilitar un acuerdo con Podemos y otras formaciones de cara a las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre. “Me propusieron como candidata entendiendo que soy una persona de consenso”, ha explicado en una entrevista en TVE, “pero se suman otras formaciones y hay otra persona que genera más consenso, estoy dispuesta a ceder”, ha asegurado. items.title: Cameroun : le Premier ministre Joseph Dion Ngute en visite à Bamenda
items.description: © DR Le chef du gouvernement est dans la capitale régionale du Nord-Ouest dès ce midi où il effectue une visite de travail de deux jours. Les habitants de la ville de Bamenda, capitale régionale du Nord-Ouest, communient les 14 et 15 octobre 2026 avec le Premier ministre. Joseph Dion Ngute effectue une visite de travail dans cette partie du pays. D’après le programme consulté par la rédaction, le chef du gouvernement va procéder au lancement du dialogue communautaire dans la région. Outre la rencontre avec les forces vives de la région, ledit programme prévoit la visite de certains sites de projets clés. Joseph Dion Ngute va ainsi accélérer l’exécution de certains projets. Entrent dans la liste des projets concernés, le siège régional des Douanes, les nouveaux bureaux du médiateur indépendant, les logement et bureaux de l’Assemblée régionale du Nord-Ouest, l’intersection Minhdu et C2D (Douanes-Lycée bilingue et route de la prison), le Carrefour de l’Ecole des champions, le nouveau marché de Bamenda I, la route du tronçon Nouveau marché de Bamenda I- Carrefour Mezam, l’Hôpital de district de Mankon nouvellement construit, entre autres. Région en proie à la crise sécuritaire depuis 10 ans, le Nord-Ouest a besoin d’une attention particulière. Il est question d’activer tous les leviers pour que cessent les hostilités et pour un retour à la paix. La visite du Premier ministre à Bamenda vient à la suite de celle effectuée à Buea, capitale régionale du Sud-Ouest, le 28 septembre 2026. A Buea, l’objectif était d’encourager les acteurs sociaux, les élites, les chefs traditionnels et la société civile à s’activer davantage pour que la paix règne dans la région du Sud-Ouest. Le Premier ministre allait aussi convaincre les combattants séparatistes actifs de déposer les armes. Les visites de Bamenda et de Buea se font alors que plusieurs attaques ont eu lieu dans les deux régions au cours du mois de septembre, mois marqué par la rentrée scolaire au Cameroun. L’enlèvement des civils, les menaces sur des civils, civils tués dans des attaques sont entre autres actes survenus ces dernières semaines. Cet article Cameroun : le Premier ministre Joseph Dion Ngute en visite à Bamenda est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Coup de tonnerre à Kiev : SpaceX bride Starlink, Zelensky critique encore le manque de soutien occidental
items.description: Le 14 octobre, Sergueï Beskrestnov, conseiller de Volodymyr Zelensky pour les technologies militaires, a confirme que SpaceX avait limite le fonctionnement des terminaux Starlink utilises par les forces ukrainiennes. Entree en vigueur dans la nuit du 13 au 14 octobre, la restriction concerne le service militaire Starshield, dont la connexion est desormais coupee lorsque les equipements se deplacent a plus de 160 km/h. « Nos forces de defense n'ont pas ete averties de cette limitation, ce qui a entraîne l'echec de plusieurs missions », affirme-t-il. Il estime egalement que la decision de l'entreprise d'Elon Musk n'a rien d'une coïncidence et la rattache a la situation politique actuelle, sans apporter de precisions sur ses motivations. Zelensky se plaint a nouveau du manque d'informations de ses allies Les restrictions de Starlink ne sont pas la seule mauvaise surprise pour Kiev. Le 13 octobre, Zelensky a deplore de ne pas avoir ete averti par ses partenaires occidentaux de nouveaux tirs de missiles balistiques russes. C'est la deuxieme fois en deux jours qu'il denonce une absence de renseignements prealables. La question du partage des informations militaires est devenue un sujet de tension entre Washington et Kiev. Zelensky affirme que des generaux ukrainiens ont ete menaces d'une interruption de cette cooperation. Ancien humoriste, il n'est pas surprenant qu'il y ait des incoherences dans son recit. Il deplore le manque d'informations de ses partenaires occidentaux, meme si « les etats-Unis continuent pour l'instant de transmettre leurs renseignements ». L'armee russe frappe huit installations energetiques et de communication Dans la nuit du 13 au 14 octobre, les forces russes ont frappe huit installations en Ukraine, dont plusieurs centrales electriques alimentant des infrastructures militaires. a Kiev, les frappes ont notamment touche le centre de donnees ATM Ukrsibbank, utilise pour la collecte de renseignements sur les forces russes, ainsi que les centrales TEC-4 et TEC-5, qui fournissaient de l'electricite aux entreprises du complexe militaro-industriel ukrainien. Dans la region de Kiev, l'armee russe a egalement atteint la centrale TEC-6, liee a l'approvisionnement d'installations logistiques militaires, la centrale thermique de Trypillia et la sous-station electrique Kievskaia. Cette derniere assurait notamment le transfert d'electricite depuis l'ouest du pays vers des installations des forces ukrainiennes. Deux autres centrales ont ete frappees dans la region de Kharkov. La Russie a parallelement fait face a une nouvelle attaque massive de drones ukrainiens. Entre 20h le 13 octobre et 8h le lendemain, les defenses antiaeriennes russes ont detruit 902 appareils, a annonce le ministere russe de la Defense. Les interceptions ont concerne une vingtaine de regions, dont celle de Moscou. La veille, 604 drones ukrainiens avaient deja ete abattus , dont 417 diriges vers la region de Moscou. En deux nuits, la defense antiaerienne russe a ainsi neutralise plus de 1 500 appareils ukrainiens.

items.title: Essence : l’Algérie, 2ème fournisseur de la France au 1er semestre 2026
items.description: D’un pays importateur, l’Algérie a changé de statut ces dernières années pour devenir un exportateur de carburants pour les véhicules, grâce à des investissements massifs dans le raffinage pétrolier. Cette position lui permet d’exporter de l’essence dans un contexte mondial marqué par une hausse vertigineuse des prix de ce carburant notamment en Europe. Parmi ses clients figure la France à qui elle a fourni 13,1 % de sa consommation d’essence durant le premier semestre 2026, selon les chiffres dévoilés par le Comité professionnel du pétrole (CPDP), publiés par l’Ufip Énergies et Mobilités et repris par le Figaro. L’Algérie se classe derrière les Pays-Bas qui occupent la première place des fournisseurs d’essence de la France avec une quantité de 627.811, soit 48% des importations. L’Italie et les Etats-Unis, avec 5,1% chacun, complètent le podium. Pétrole : l’Algérie dans le top 5 des fournisseurs de la France En plus de l’essence, l’Algérie figure aussi parmi les principaux fournisseurs de pétrole à la France. Durant les six premiers mois de l’année 2026, sa part des importations françaises de brut était de 7,7%. En Afrique, elle est devancée par le Nigéria avec 11,4%n alors que les Etats-Unis sont largement en tête avec une part considérable de 28,2% des importations françaises d’or noir durant le premier semestre de l’année en cours. Le Kazakhstan arrive derrière avec 15,5%. Malgré la crise politique qui a fortement ébranlé les relations entre les deux pays de juillet 2024 jusqu’à février 2026, la France a poursuivi ses importations de pétrole, de gaz et de carburants d’Algérie qui tire profit de la hausse des prix de l’essence sur le marché mondial. Cette crise a lourdement pesé sur les échanges commerciaux entre les deux pays. Alors qu’ils étaient de 11,2 milliards d’euros en 2024, ils ont chuté sous 9 milliards d’euros à 8,9 milliards entre juillet 2025 et juin 2026. L’article Essence : l’Algérie, 2ème fournisseur de la France au 1er semestre 2026 est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Preparing for 2027 Board and Executive Conversations
items.description: By Ernest De-Graft Egyir Insight. Effective board and executive discussions begin with clear evidence, honest assessment, and well-defined strategic choices. As CEOs prepare for 2027, they must ensure that discussions about organizational performance and future direction are supported by credible information and a realistic understanding of risks and opportunities. The objective is not merely to present results. It is to create a shared understanding of the decisions, investments, and governance priorities required to move the organization forward. Key Strategies: 1. Prepare a clear assessment of year-to-date performance against strategic objectives. 2. Identify material risks, emerging opportunities, and unresolved challenges. 3. Develop realistic strategic options for the year ahead. 4. Clarify the decisions and guidance required from the board. 5. Ensure that proposed priorities are supported by credible analysis and resource plans. CEO Leadership Actions. Prepare a concise and evidence-based assessment of the organization’s current position. Identify the most important strategic questions requiring board and executive attention. Ensure that proposed 2027 priorities are consistent with the organization’s risk appetite, capabilities, and financial position. Actionable Tip. *Before your next board or executive strategy discussion, prepare a one-page brief covering performance, key risks, growth opportunities, proposed priorities, and decisions required. Why This Matters? Strong board and executive conversations improve strategic alignment and decision quality. When CEOs present a clear view of performance and future choices, they enable more productive oversight, better resource allocation, and stronger organizational readiness for 2027. About the Author. Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and served on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee.

items.title: UE-Royaume-Uni : un deuxième sommet à Bruxelles pour renforcer la coopération post-Brexit
items.description: L'Union européenne et le Royaume-Uni se retrouvent le 20 novembre à Bruxelles pour leur deuxième sommet bilatéral, avec pour objectif d'approfondir leur coopération économique et sécuritaire, six ans après le retrait britannique du bloc européen. Cette rencontre de haut niveau sera l'occasion de dresser le bilan des avancées enregistrées depuis le premier sommet, organisé le 19 mai 2025 à Londres, et de définir les prochaines étapes d'un partenariat que les deux parties souhaitent renforcer dans plusieurs domaines stratégiques, notamment l'économie, la défense, l'énergie, le climat et la migration. Le sommet intervient dans un contexte marqué par une volonté affichée de Londres et de Bruxelles de resserrer leurs liens, face aux défis sécuritaires et économiques auxquels l'Europe est confrontée. « L'UE et le Royaume-Uni sont des partenaires partageant les mêmes valeurs et des intérêts communs. Notre sécurité et notre prospérité sont étroitement liées », a souligné le président du Conseil européen, Antonio Costa, plaidant pour un « partenariat solide » entre les deux parties. « En approfondissant notre coopération, nous pouvons renforcer notre capacité à relever les défis, consolider notre résilience et promouvoir la stabilité en Europe et au-delà », a souligné M. Costa lors de l'annonce, lundi dernier, de la tenue de cette deuxième réunion de haut niveau. Le premier sommet UE-Royaume-Uni avait marqué une nouvelle étape dans les relations bilatérales, avec la conclusion d'accords destinés à consolider le partenariat, notamment dans les domaines de la sécurité et de la défense. A cette occasion, les deux parties s'étaient engagées à poursuivre leurs travaux sur de futurs accords concernant l'énergie, les échanges agroalimentaires, le climat, la mobilité des personnes et les migrations. Les discussions du 20 novembre devraient notamment porter sur la simplification des formalités applicables aux échanges de produits agroalimentaires, les systèmes d'échange de quotas d'émission de carbone et l'interconnexion des réseaux énergétiques. La mobilité des jeunes et le renforcement de la coopération contre l'immigration irrégulière figurent également parmi les dossiers sur la table des dirigeants des deux parties. Sur le plan économique, l'Exécutif britannique estime que les accords envisagés pourraient générer plus de 10 milliards de livres sterling par an pour l'économie du Royaume-Uni d'ici à 2040, notamment grâce à la réduction des obstacles aux échanges commerciaux. Le Premier ministre britannique, Andy Burnham, a lui aussi plaidé pour un rapprochement avec l'UE. Devant la Chambre des communes, il a appelé récemment à l'ouverture d'un « dialogue sérieux » sur l'avenir des relations entre les deux parties, estimant que le maintien du statu quo ne répondait plus pleinement aux intérêts du Royaume-Uni. Depuis son arrivée à Downing Street en juillet, le dirigeant britannique a exprimé à maintes reprises sa volonté de resserrer les liens avec Bruxelles, affirmant également qu'un retour du Royaume-Uni au sein de l'UE faisait partie des options envisageables. Depuis le retrait britannique en 2020, les relations entre Bruxelles et Londres s'appuient notamment sur l’accord de retrait, le cadre de Windsor et l'accord de commerce et de coopération. Ces textes constituent le socle des relations post-Brexit et encadrent les échanges entre les deux capitales. Lors de leur premier sommet, les deux parties avaient convenu aussi de se réunir chaque année afin d'assurer un suivi régulier de leur coopération. La rencontre de novembre à Bruxelles doit s'inscrire dans cette dynamique et permettre d'identifier de nouvelles pistes de collaboration, alors que l'UE et le Royaume-Uni cherchent à mieux coordonner leurs efforts face aux enjeux communs. The post UE-Royaume-Uni : un deuxième sommet à Bruxelles pour renforcer la coopération post-Brexit appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Hunger changed my mind — Timini Egbuson on embracing YouTube movies
items.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nollywood actor Timini Egbuson has reflected on his changing perception of YouTube movies, joking that he might have struggled financially had he continued to look down on productions made for the video-sharing platform. Egbuson shared the thought in a post on X Tuesday night, writing, “Can’t believe I was looking down on YouTube movies at some point. Hunger go don kpai me by now.” His remark highlights the growing commercial appeal of YouTube movies in Nigeria’s entertainment industry, where actors and filmmakers are increasingly using the platform to reach audiences and generate revenue from their productions. Egbuson, who has now featured in YouTube movie productions, has embraced the growing market, adding to his work across Nollywood’s film and streaming landscape. Many Nollywood actors have long prioritised cinema movies, often seeing them as more prestigious and commercially rewarding than YouTube productions. As a result, some overlook online films, despite their growing audiences and earning potential. However, the success of YouTube movies is gradually changing perceptions within the industry. Reports show that Nigerian filmmakers were increasingly turning to YouTube amid the pullback by global streaming companies, with the platform offering easier access to audiences and fewer barriers to distribution. The post Hunger changed my mind — Timini Egbuson on embracing YouTube movies appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia 'totally unacceptable', says Dar
items.description: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Wednesday said that Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia were “totally unacceptable”. He made the remarks while addressing a joint press conference alongside Omani Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr Albusaidi, who is currently on an official visit to Pakistan, following the eighth session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC). At the outset of the press conference, Dar said that the two sides would sign a protocol relating to the commission. He said that this reflected “a shared resolve to further strengthen and expand bilateral cooperation in areas of mutual interest”. He said that the two sides would also sign an agreement for mutual visa exemption for holders of diplomatic and official passports. “Pakistan-Oman friendship remains strong and forward-looking,” he told media. The two ministers would after the press conference sign “a number of bilateral agreements”, Dar said. He added that the two ministers had also agreed to hold a business-to-business investment forum in Pakistan. The ministers discussed the situation in Gulf as well, he said, adding that “Pakistan remained committed to contributing constructively to diplomatic efforts aimed at promoting peace and stability in the region”. Dar said that the two sides also exchanged views on recent Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. He said that he conveyed Pakistan’s condemnation of the attacks. “I underscored that attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure are totally unacceptable. My brother [Albusaidi] actually fully endorses this. Violations of international law pose a serious threat to regional peace and security,” he said. “I reaffirmed Pakistan’s full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and our unwavering commitment to the kingdom’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security in accordance with the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement,” he said. They also “emphasised the urgent need for unhindered delivery of humanitarian assistance to the people of Gaza”, Dar said. DPM Dar also stressed that India’s unilateral abeyance of the Indus Water Treaty was “a material breach of international law”. “This action threatens the water, food and energy security of Pakistan’s 250 million people,” Dar said. Speaking at the occasion, Albusaidi said the JMC had “provided an important opportunity to review the state of bilateral relations”. He said that two sides “reaffirmed the strength of the longstanding ties” between the two countries. “Both Oman and Pakistan attach great importance to dialogue and diplomacy as essential means of addressing regional challenges, easing tensions and promoting peace and stability,” Albusaidi said. He also appreciated Pakistan’s diplomatic role in the US-Iran war . He reaffirmed the two countries’ “shared commitment to further deepening our bilateral partnership and broadening cooperation across centres of mutual benefit”. The two countries agreed that dialogue and diplomacy were “the only way forward” to resolve regional conflicts, Dar said in response to a reporter’s question. “We are both on the same page,” he said. Meanwhile, Dar told reporters that a free trade agreement between Pakistan and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) would help expand business activities, adding that he was told that barring one, all countries had consented to the agreement. Responding to a question about the gaps in between bilateral talks between the two countries, Dar said Albusaidi’s visit was previously delayed because Pakistan had been involved in mediation efforts between US and Iran. Albusaidi added that discussions had continued “behind the scenes”. Responding to a question about the Strait of Hormuz, Albusaidi said that Oman was committed to “unhindered navigation” through the strait “because of its vitality to the global economy and the region”. Dar commends Albusaidi’s efforts towards regional peace Albusaidi arrived in Pakistan on Tuesday on a two-day visit. Speaking at the outset of the 8th session of the JMC, Dar said the two had “worked out” certain areas of bilateral interest and discussed global issues in detail, including the US-Iran war, the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, Bab al-Mandab and Gaza in their restricted meeting. Dar said the two sides had also discussed Jammu and Kashmir and other pressing regional issues. He commended Albusaidi’s leadership and efforts towards regional peace in the Middle East. “I personally greatly admire your efforts. I know how much hard work you have put in,” he said, noting that Pakistan’s position on the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) was “very unique”. “We are members of both the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and, obviously, the United Nations and other multilateral bodies,” Dar said. He stressed, “There should not be any long gaps between bilateral engagements,” noting potential in the areas of trade, economic activities and investment opportunities. Dar said he had promised to visit Oman in 2027 to hold the next session of the commission there. He added that both sides had identified areas of mutual interest and discussed possible meetings. He said Pakistan and Oman cooperated closely and cordially, adding that although their diplomatic relations had completed 55 years, their ties went back “centuries”. Dar said the two countries shared a history of “love and affection”, particularly in relation to Balochistan and Gwadar. Referring to discussions on Bab al-Mandeb and recent developments involving the Houthis and Saudi Arabia, Dar said both sides shared similar views on resolving regional issues. He said the impact of regional tensions was also visible in Pakistan, where energy supply chains had been affected, and fuel prices had skyrocketed, adding that the “common man could not afford the resulting burden.” Speaking on the occasion, Albusaidi said Oman was committed to further strengthening bilateral engagement and cooperation in various fields that could bring greater benefits to the people of both countries. “I am delighted to be here with my delegation in Islamabad this morning, in this very warm, friendly and brotherly country, Pakistan, with which, as you have rightly said, we share bonds of history, culture, tradition and unity,” he said. He said the Pakistan-Oman JMC was one of the mechanisms for exploring further avenues of collaboration, adding that the two countries also had a business council and a political consultation mechanism between their foreign ministers. “We can do much more, and as we made a joint commitment this morning to make this meeting a success, I believe the more we do, the more we can deliver on the promise and the aspiration of our leaderships and our people,” Albusaidi said. He also commended Pakistan’s role in supporting dialogue and diplomacy in the region. “Your efforts to encourage engagement, understanding, respect and recognition are commendable, and I salute you for all your efforts,” he said, adding that Oman greatly appreciated Pakistan’s role in providing space for dialogue between Iran and the US. Albusaidi said there was significant potential for economic cooperation between Oman and Pakistan, particularly in trade, logistics, port connectivity, energy and food security. “The potential exists, and our task is to remove any obstacles and create the conditions that allow businesses to thrive so that we can fully benefit from this potential,” he said. He also called for greater cooperation in tourism, academic and technological fields, as well as more regular exchanges between the people of the two countries. “Once again, I appreciate the efforts of our private sector and industrial partners,” Albusaidi said, adding that he looked forward to further discussions on strengthening bilateral cooperation. Dar, Omani FM call for sustained bilateral engagement Earlier in the day, Dar held a meeting with Albusaidi ahead of the JMC session, the Foreign Office (FO) said. The two ministers reaffirmed the close, fraternal ties between Pakistan and Oman and underscored the importance of sustained high-level engagement to deepen cooperation in areas of mutual interest, particularly trade, investment and people-to-people contacts, according to the FO. “The two sides also exchanged views on regional developments and emphasised the importance of dialogue and diplomacy in advancing lasting peace and stability”, the FO said. Albusaidi commended Pakistan’s efforts to promote regional peace and security, while Dar acknowledged and appreciated Oman’s constructive role and shared aspirations for regional peace and stability, the statement added. A day earlier, the Foreign Office (FO) said the JMC session would review the entire spectrum of Pakistan-Oman bilateral relations and strengthen cooperation. The visit “reflects the longstanding fraternal relations between Pakistan and Oman and is expected to further deepen mutually beneficial cooperation Last week, DPM Dar chaired an inter-ministerial meeting in Islamabad to review preparations for the upcoming JMC session, according to state-run Radio Pakistan. The meeting reviewed the agenda, bilateral agreements, and arrangements for the co-chairing of the JMC session, it said.

items.title: World Cup Visa Scandal: There is no ‘justification’ to dismiss me – Kofi Adams
items.description: Minister for Sports and Recreation Kofi Adams has rejected calls by the Minority in Parliament for his dismissal over an alleged visa scandal linked to the FIFA World Cup. About 90 people reportedly paid between $10,000 and $15,000 each, but only five of them obtained visas for the global showpiece, which was staged in the USA, Canada and Mexico. Yaw Ampofo Ankrah has already been suspended as National Sports Authority (NSA) boss, and further heads are expected to roll at the Sports Ministry as the Presidency is set to launch a probe into the matter, JoySports can confirm. When asked about calls for his removal, Adams said: “Government money has not been lost,” he told Citi News. “Well, I don’t see the justification. Both the American Embassy and TRIBE Culture Fest, the NSA and the GTA were doing their thing behind the Ministry. The Ministry didn’t know. “The first time I ever sat and had a conversation in relation to that matter was when the May 19 letter requested the forwarding of event coordinators and volunteers to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Embassy. That’s when I got to know the details of what was happening.”

items.title: Djeneba Keita Hann préside le Conseil d’affaires tuniso-guinéen
items.description: Le Tunisia Africa Business Council (TABC) a conduit, du 6 au 11 octobre 2026 à Conakry, une mission économique multisectorielle réunissant une délégation de 30 entreprises tunisiennes, avec la participation du Tunisia Consortium for African Development (Tucad). Cette mission a associé rencontres d’affaires, échanges institutionnels, workshop sur le financement des projets, lancement du Conseil d’affaires tuniso-guinéen et participation à la troisième édition du Forum pour la Croissance Inclusive en Afrique (Focia). Mobilisant des entreprises actives notamment dans les infrastructures, le BTP, l’énergie, l’eau et l’assainissement, l’industrie, la santé, l’ingénierie, les technologies de l’information et les services, cette mission visait à développer les partenariats tuniso-guinéens et à positionner l’expertise tunisienne sur les priorités de développement de la Guinée, notamment celles du Programme Simandou 2040. Le 7 octobre, une journée de rencontres B2B et B2G au Noom Hotel Conakry a permis aux membres de la délégation d’échanger avec des opérateurs économiques et des représentants institutionnels guinéens. Ces rendez-vous ont favorisé l’identification de besoins, de complémentarités et de pistes de coopération commerciale, technique et industrielle. Les 8 et 9 octobre, le programme s’est poursuivi par des visites et des rencontres auprès d’institutions publiques et d’acteurs privés. Les échanges menés par TABC, Tucad et les membres de la délégation tunisienne ont notamment concerné Aboubacar Kourouma, ministre du Commerce, de l’Industrie et des PME, autour des perspectives de développement des échanges commerciaux, des partenariats industriels et de la coopération entre PME tunisiennes et guinéennes.Avec Facinet Sylla, ministre des Infrastructures, la rencontre a permis d’explorer les possibilités de mobilisation de l’ingénierie et du savoir-faire tunisiens dans les projets d’infrastructures et les grands chantiers de développement. Avec Kadé Camara, directrice générale adjointe en charge de l’attractivité et du rayonnement de la Guinée au Guinea Development Board, on a examiné les synergies en matière d’investissement, d’accompagnement des entreprises et d’identification de projets. Mamoudou Nagnalen Barry, président du CA de la Compagnie du TransGuinéen (CTG) a discuté avec les membres de la délégation tunisienne les opportunités de coopération liées aux infrastructures ferroviaires, portuaires et logistiques et à leur effet d’entraînement sur l’économie guinéenne. Avec Mamadou Angelo Diallo, délégué général de la Delivery Unit – Unité d’exécution du programme Simandou 2040, les échanges ont porté sur les priorités du programme et les possibilités de contribution des entreprises tunisiennes à sa mise en œuvre. Les rencontres avec les acteurs privés guinéens ont également permis de rapprocher les entreprises des deux pays et d’explorer des collaborations adaptées aux besoins du marché. Le 8 octobre, Jade Advisory, membre de Tucad, a organisé, en partenariat avec le Guinea Development Board, un workshop intitulé «Mobiliser le secteur privé pour la mise en œuvre du Programme Simandou 2040 – De l’ambition à la bancabilité» . Consacré aux partenariats public-privé et à la structuration du financement des projets, cet atelier a placé au centre des échanges les conditions nécessaires pour transformer les ambitions de développement en projets susceptibles de mobiliser des investisseurs et des financements. Un moment majeur de la mission a été la création officielle, le 9 octobre au Noom Hotel Conakry, du Conseil d’affaires tuniso-guinéen (CATG),lors d’une cérémonie suivie d’un cocktail de networking réunissant des personnalités institutionnelles et des représentants du secteur privé des deux pays. Le CATG est présidé par Djeneba Keita Hann, accompagnée de Almamy Camara en qualité de vice-président et de Abou Sidibé en qualité de secrétaire général. Il constitue un cadre permanent de dialogue, de mise en relation et de suivi des opportunités d’affaires, destiné à renforcer les échanges commerciaux, les investissements et le développement de projets conjoints entre la Tunisie et la Guinée. Le 10 octobre, la délégation tunisienne a participé à la 3 e édition du Forum pour la croissance inclusive en Afrique (Focia).Anis Jaziri, président de TABC et de Tucad, et Sami Driss, vice-président de TABC et Ceo de Comet Group, y sont intervenus. M. Jaziri a pris part au panel consacré aux investissements et chaînes de valeur africaines, consacré au financement, aux partenariats et aux opportunités, et M. Driss est intervenu dans le panel consacré à la transformation locale, à la captation de valeur et aux opportunités d’industrialisation en Afrique. Participation qui a inscrit la contribution tunisienne dans les réflexions sur le financement du développement, la coopération entre entreprises africaines et la construction de chaînes de valeur compétitives. À l’issue de cette mission, TABC entend poursuivre, avec Tucad, le CATG et ses partenaires guinéens, le suivi des contacts établis et des opportunités identifiées afin de les traduire en partenariats opérationnels et en projets concrets. L’article Djeneba Keita Hann préside le Conseil d’affaires tuniso-guinéen est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Automating death: Israel’s AI-powered genocide in Gaza
items.description: On February 29, 2024, Israeli forces fired at civilians as they gathered around an aid convoy. At least 115 people were killed in what has since become known as the ‘Flour Massacre’. Survivors recalled the involvement of armed tanks and quadcopters. “When the aid entered, the tank and quadcopter started firing at the people gathered, the people who went to get food for themselves and their children. They started shooting at them,” Mahmoud Ahmad, a Gaza resident, told Reuters shortly after the incident. Screenshot from video released by Israeli forces/Anadolu Agency Powered by artificial intelligence (AI), Israel’s strategy of keeping soldiers “out of harm’s way” while they kill Palestinians relies on quadcopter drones and various AI systems to identify and target people. Quadcopters such as the ‘Bird of Prey’ — designed by Elbit Systems, the apartheid state’s largest arms manufacturer — have contributed to the deaths of Palestinians in Gaza, where more than 70,000 people have reportedly been killed since the beginning of the genocide. According to the manufacturer, the ‘Bird of Prey’ quadcopter drone is designed to enable “fast and accurate” targeting and is light enough to fit into a soldier’s backpack. The drone can transmit high-quality footage in real time, facilitating precision targeting. According to the Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor , at least 60 civilians have been killed by fire or munitions dropped from these drones since the October 2025 ceasefire till early September 2026. In April 2024, reports surfaced online of drones playing sounds of crying babies and screaming women and children to lure residents and kill them. Palestinians inspect the site of a house targeted by Israeli airstrikes after the Israeli military warned residents to evacuate late on Saturday, in Al-Zawayda, central Gaza Strip on October 11, 2026. —Reuters Lavender According to Palestinian-Israeli news outlet +972 Magazine , the Lavender system was designed to identify suspected members of the military wings of Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ) as potential targets for air strikes. The publication reported that human oversight of the system was minimal, with one intelligence officer describing his role as little more than a “stamp of approval” for attacks. According to the report, Lavender’s accuracy was estimated at 90 per cent, meaning that around 10 per cent of those it identified as targets were incorrectly classified. The report also said that, during the early weeks of the war, Israeli military officials permitted strikes against suspected junior-level fighters even when they risked killing up to 15 to 20 civilians. The report alleged that these policies facilitated attacks that caused extensive civilian casualties in Gaza. “They could target someone who is a photography personnel or a truck driver and take another 15 people down with him,” a testimonial on Breaking the Silence — a digital archive of Israeli atrocities against Palestinians — revealed. Twenty seconds. That’s the time given to consider whether a target should be bombed and if that target is male. The Israeli army’s use of AI systems such as Lavender further enabled blanket targeting of Palestinians. Another entry spoke of how a single target could result in hundreds of ‘casualties’. “That they knowingly authorised a strike. I don’t know what number they authorised exactly, but they knew it would be more than a hundred [civilian deaths].” The entries dated 2023 are an astonishing admission of targeted strikes on civilians. Where’s Daddy? ‘Where’s Daddy?’ is an automated system used to track people and identify them for targeting when they enter their homes. According to reports, the system was designed to target individuals at their residences. It has been linked to the deaths of thousands of civilians, including women and children. “It’s much easier to bomb a family’s home,” an Israeli officer told +972 Magazine . Habsora A third system, Habsora, also known as ‘The Gospel’, was designed to identify buildings and infrastructure allegedly linked to Hamas for targeting. Israel has accused the Palestinian group of using essential infrastructure, including hospitals, schools, UNRWA buildings and mosques, for military purposes. These allegations have been disputed, and the resulting attacks have caused extensive destruction across the besieged enclave, where approximately 82 per cent of buildings have reportedly been damaged or destroyed. Who is responsible for these AI controlled attacks? The Israeli military’s main intelligence unit, Unit 8200, has been at the centre of cyberwarfare. The unit was established in 1948, the same year the state of Israel was founded. From its inception, Israel has developed mechanisms of surveillance and control. Other systems include facial recognition systems such as Red Wolf and Blue Wolf. A 2020 testimony published by Breaking the Silence describes Israeli soldiers photographing Palestinians’ identity cards and compiling a database for the Blue Wolf system. Blue Wolf then displays different colours depending on whether it recognises an individual. A yellow light gives Israeli forces the option to detain that person, while a red light signals that they should be arrested. In its 2023 report, Israel and Occupied Palestinian Territories: Automated Apartheid: How Facial Recognition Fragments, Segregates and Controls Palestinians in the OPT , Amnesty International found that Israeli soldiers used a gamified system to map Palestinian identities. Soldiers were reportedly rewarded for photographing Palestinians without their consent. In 2024, Muhammad Ahmad Odeh recounted to Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor how a quadcopter killed his sister in Gaza and described what happened afterwards. “After just two or three hours, a small aircraft flew in and took pictures of us inside the house. The army forces then moved in and started shooting at us. They fired sound shots, causing a state of panic among the women and children.” Terror beyond Palestine Ambulances arrive at American University of Beirut Medical Center (AUBMC) as more than 1,000 people, including Hezbollah fighters and medics, were wounded when the pagers they use to communicate exploded across Lebanon, according to a security source, in Beirut, Lebanon on September 17, 2024. —Reuters/File Israel’s AI warfare systems have been used beyond Gaza and the occupied West Bank. The Israeli Defence Forces (IDF) employed some of the same AI-enabled software in its war against Lebanon. According to Israeli military Chief of Staff Lt Gen Eyal Zamir, the Unmanned Systems and Artificial Intelligence Branch is scheduled to become operational in December 2026. The new branch will be responsible for further developing and deploying the Israeli state’s various AI-powered and unmanned systems. Image header: People walk at a site destroyed during the Israeli offensive, in Beit Lahiya, in the northern Gaza Strip on August 18, 2026. —Reuters/File

items.title: The Most Cursed Team in American Sports
items.description: The mythical story of the Buffalo Bills could be told like this: Their fans are crazy and live in the snow. They shovel this snow out of their stadium to help their godforsaken football team, which, until recently, was most famous for losing the Super Bowl four times in a row in the early 1990s. According to one theory, those failures fed into Timothy McVeigh’s derangement before he planned and executed the Oklahoma City bombing. The franchise was an utter disaster, for the most part, until the 2018 arrival of an otherworldly quarterback named Josh Allen, who has exhibited many heroics. But he has yet to bring his team to the Super Bowl. Four of his playoff runs have ended with haunting losses to the quarterback Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. The others were cut short in unromantic fashion—­most recently by one of the sloppier performances of Allen’s career, against the Denver Broncos. From the outside, you might ask: “Can he really do it?” But in Buffalo, the words Josh Allen come out like “Good morning.” On a Sunday afternoon in September, I sat down in an ancient tavern near the Buffalo River to eat chicken wings and watch the Bills’ division rivals, the New England Patriots, play the Pittsburgh Steelers. An older man joined me and asked, unprompted, if I liked Josh Allen. “Who doesn’t?” I said. He revealed that he was wearing a Josh Allen shirt under his sweater, said that he would get another one for me out of his car, and then did. Josh Allen is everywhere in Buffalo. He appears in murals and on billboards; road signs are doctored to feature his name and face. At the grocery store, you can buy Josh Allen Crunch Time cereal and cantaloupes grown on the Allen family’s farm, in Firebaugh, California. There is hardly a business in the city that does not possess at least one life-size cutout of the man. (Shortly after I left, an 11-story banner of him went up downtown.) In a parking lot near the team’s brand-new Highmark Stadium, I chatted with Jenny Kless, a kind-eyed woman who tailgates out of a refurbished Volkswagen bus. When it came time to talk about Josh Allen, she put her hand over her heart. “What a beautiful person he is,” she said, and assured me that Bills fans believe he can do anything. “I’m gonna spell that for you: B-I-L-L-I-E-V-E.” I found Andy Dikens and Gary Thomas tailgating by a Tesla Cybertruck. They told me they’d been following the team since the ’80s and now had the same opinion on Josh Allen, which they expressed in tandem: Dikens : He’s a stud. Thomas : He’s the best player in the league. Dikens : Best player in the league by far. Thomas : Definitely a stud, I agree. Leo Roth, a longtime sports columnist for the Democrat and Chronicle in Rochester, about 60 miles east, told me that Allen is the best player Buffalo has ever had, and claimed that even Jim Kelly, the first-ballot Hall of Fame quarterback who led the Bills to those four consecutive Super Bowls, would agree. (When I emailed Kelly to confirm, he answered, “Yes, I’m not scared to admit that.”) As many sports people see it, Roth said, Allen may be the team’s best, last hope of redemption. “If you can’t win it with this guy,” they say, “you probably never will.” To saddle one man with the hopes and dreams of an entire city is a heady gamble with, well, the hopes and dreams of an entire city. But Buffalo’s circumstances may inspire a little shooting-for-the-moon. It’s a highly segregated, economically stagnant, postindustrial city that has been struggling for decades. Buffalo has a fascinating history and many great qualities; it would be unfair and inaccurate to say the people there have nothing but football. Yet football plainly matters far more to its modern-day sense of self than anything else. Robert Thompson, a professor of television and popular culture at Syracuse University who has lived in the area for 30 years, was the first person I spoke with who directly acknowledged the risks involved in belief. “I suppose I look at Josh Allen like I would look at an economy that was based on one agricultural product,” he said. In that situation, you have to pray. The Bills’ new , $2 billion stadium, a gigantic silver spaceship plopped among converted mills and manufacturing plants, was partly paid for by Erie County and New York State taxpayers; the state leased the place to the team’s owners, Terry and Kim Pegula (who also own the Buffalo Sabres). The stadium is named—as its predecessor was—for a health-­insurance company. Inside, the design and decor nod to local folkways, most notably in the form of a 20-foot sculpture of a broken folding table —the cheap kind that you would buy for a backyard barbecue or school fund­raiser. This is a monument to a Buffalo tradition. Sometime in the 2010s, fans began body-slamming foldable tables at tailgates. Although now understood as something people do in good humor, because they are drunk and love the Bills so much, that’s not how the ritual started. “They were doing stuff like that because the team was so bad,” Mike Catalana, the sports director of the ABC affiliate in Rochester, told me. They needed to entertain themselves somehow. My husband’s childhood friend Dan, whose family is from Buffalo, put it differently: The table-breaking habit was a display of dark humor—­half-ironic self-harm carried out by people who were miserable. I grew up in a small town south of Rochester, which also gets a good deal of lake-effect snow. Still, I remember a general feeling that our neighbor city was full of eccentrics who, for un­fathomable reasons, had chosen to live in a depressed Arctic-like region rather than someplace normal. The Bills were part of their sad lot. We had some true-blue fans in my hometown, but in general our community regarded the Bills with a degree of remove—we wished them well, but we didn’t necessarily want to get involved. My classmates instead concocted reasons to root for better teams: the Steelers, the Patriots, the Colts. Today, many people I grew up with are now Bills Mafia. But I know—and they know—it wasn’t always so. I don’t begrudge anybody their porch flags or bumper stickers, however they behaved in decades past. The spirit is catching, and what else are you going to do? A couple of Christmases ago, my uncle—a farmer who is known locally for his Bing Crosby eyes and sometimes-mean-­spirited sense of humor—told me that he’d been rooting against the Bills because he didn’t like to see other people getting so excited. But, he said, he’d had to stop. Even he couldn’t root against a guy like Josh Allen. On paper, the Bills’ chances may be better than they’ve ever been before. (By week four of this season, the Vegas odds were giving them the best shot at winning the Super Bowl.) The Bills’ defense has gotten younger and faster; they traded for the very talented wide receiver DJ Moore. Many of the fans I met in Buffalo suggested that Allen is also getting better—that he’s more mature as a player and a human being, having married the actor Hailee Steinfeld and become a family man. They love her too, and call her the queen of Buffalo. By the week of my visit, the Bills had already won their first game of the season, in Houston, on a touchdown throw from Allen after the two-­minute warning. Now they were set to play the Detroit Lions, in what would be the first-ever regular-season game in a stadium that all manner of T-shirts call The House That Josh Built . A few controversies about the building had already emerged—fan backlash against the soaring cost of attendance, a confusing sod debacle —but in the tailgate areas on Thursday afternoon, people were simply amped and optimistic. When I arrived at Hammer’s Lot, a popular site down the street from both the remnants of the old stadium and its gleaming replacement, the first person I saw was shirtless and, frankly, pantsless. He wore a gladiator-style skirt constructed entirely out of Labatt Blue boxes. I’d guess that 80 percent of the men were wearing Josh Allen jerseys. But the crowd was diverse. I saw super-pregnant women in red-and-blue zebra-striped leggings, older women in red-and-blue-bedazzled jeans, and teen girls in sweatshirts with red and blue hearts on the sleeves. There are some generational divides and hints of factions within the Bills fandom, and you might sketch the boundaries of these groups based on their relationship to this parking lot. The longtime owner, local resident Eric Matwijow, is beloved by a huge crowd of regulars; he claims that some of them have spread their family members’ ashes on his gravel. Matwijow also told me that “woke” or “nose ring” Bills fans do not like him. Nor do the table-slammers, because Hammer’s Lot prohibits that activity (on account of its being dangerous and stupid). He also openly resents the people who call themselves the “Bills Mafia” because he is old enough to remember the actual Mafia in Buffalo, which, as he mentioned to me, was all about murder and torture and stealing and other crimes. To be fair, Del Reid, a 50-year-old former web developer, coined the term Bills Mafia accidentally, in 2011. It was a tongue-in-cheek response during a Twitter feud with a sports reporter that took on a life of its own. Reid and Matwijow have very different styles and a degree of personal animosity, but they come together on one thing, which is, of course, Josh Allen. Neither was bothered that their hometown quarterback is from California. He’s not from California California, they each separately explained, but from the Central Valley. He’s “not a surfer dude,” Reid told me. “He’s a farm boy,” Matwijow said. The way they talked about him reminded me of how A. Bartlett Giamatti once described New Yorkers’ feelings toward the great Mets pitcher Tom Seaver, who also came east from California, bringing miracles. “He contrasted completely with the part of the country he was known to come from,” Giamatti, a future baseball commissioner, wrote in 1977. People who had little in common with Seaver loved him because he was “a working guy who got rewarded,” “who went by the rules and made it.” Although Allen isn’t a Buffalo native, he fits in as though he were, Reid added. “We love him, and he loves us back.” I n the plaza in front of Highmark Stadium, enormous steel bison puffed steam from their nostrils. Inside the stadium, the energy was even more rock-and-roll. Before the game, an introductory video declared the new Highmark “a beacon of blue-collar football built for Buffalo, by Buffalo.” The crowd’s full-throated celebration was followed by the boom of fireworks. More than 60,000 attendees had been given light-up bracelets that were designed to flash red, white, and blue at dramatic moments, such as when Allen ran onto the field for the first time. The Bills loped down the field on their opening drive, which ended with Allen running for a touchdown and the Jumbotron instructing everyone to sing “The Bills make me want to SHOUT!” The Bills scored another touchdown on their next drive, and we stood to “SHOUT!” again. When Allen ran it in toward the end of the third quarter, we were on our fifth rendition. The final score was 41–31, and the Bills were 2–0 by midnight. “I can’t wait to watch the highlights,” a woman in front of me said, with a sigh, to a friend as we walked to our cars. Just before I left Buffalo, I sat with my laptop in the café section of a Wegmans—where customers could impulse-buy a chunk of turf from the old stadium for $99.99—and listened to the old men nearby chat about the game over coffee and doughnuts. It was good news and bad news. Allen looked perfect, but the defense needs to gel, they said. Things were going well, but nobody knows what will happen in a long season. Sports are sick and twisted. Even the hottest start can fizzle out, as Buffalonians know in their bones. (They would lose to the Patriots in week four.) The Bills curse is vague. The fans feel cursed, but they have never settled on the place to pin this feeling. One theory holds that Buffalo is destined to lose because President William McKinley was assassinated in the city, at the Pan-American Exposition in 1901. Mark Poloncarz, the county executive who helped negotiate the terms for the new stadium, told me that he’d joined Mayor Sean Ryan to lay a wreath at a monument to McKinley in downtown Buffalo this year, and that Ryan had asked McKinley to release the city from his vengeance. Other theories about the Bills’ misfortune involve more classic stuff—for instance, that the old stadium had been placed nearly on top of a small cemetery, and occupied land that once belonged to Native Americans. (The new stadium is at least 1,000 feet from the cemetery and has signage that acknowledges the Seneca Nation.) Phil Passafiume, a Buffalo fan I spoke with in Hammer’s Lot, suggested one more factor: The old Highmark had featured O. J. Simpson on a wall among the team’s other legends; the new one leaves him off. The city and team have addressed so many of their potential curses this year; if the Bills finally do win, they’ll never know which one was really the source of their troubles. That their day of triumph will come, this year or sometime soon, feels inevitable to me—if only because it’s too dark to imagine otherwise. The Sunday after my trip, as I sat in a Brooklyn sports bar watching the Bills with my hands pressed to my face, fully converted to the cause, I thought back to what Roth, the newspaper columnist, had said about Josh Allen: “If you can’t win it with this guy, you probably never will.” Knock on wood and God forbid. *Illustration source images: Kevin Sabitus / Getty; Bryan M. Bennett / Getty; Ric Tapia / Getty; Juan Alejandro Bernal / Shutterstock; Quintin Soloviev / Wikimedia. This article appears in the December 2026 print edition with the headline “The Most Cursed Team in American Sports.”

items.title: Diphtheria: Kano disease control centre confirms 5 family members dead
items.description: The Kano State Centre for Disease Control (KNCDC), has confirmed the death of five children from the same family as a result of diphtheria in Danbare Ward, Layin Dutse, Kumbotso Local Government Area. The Centre’s Director-General, Prof. Muhammad Adamu-Abbas, confirmed this in a statement on Tuesday. Adamu-Abbas, who confirmed the deaths based on the case definition and verbal autopsy, also attributed the deaths of the children to late presentation of the case to the health facility and zero dose. He said the ages of the deceased children range between one year to 13 years. “The investigation confirmed a cluster of six children linked to one family. Tragically, five of the six children died due to late presentation. “The sixth child, Ummahabila Ibrahim, four years, was admitted on Oct. 1, 2026 with mild diphtheria and discharged on Oct. 4, 2026. A follow-up on Oct. 12, 2026, confirmed she is completely fine and healthy. “Clinical presentations included fever, sore throat, difficulty swallowing, neck swelling, nasal bleeding/regurgitation, and white patches on the tonsils (pseudomembrane). According to him, assessments included severe diphtheria, thrombocytopenia, anaemia, neuropathy, and risk of upper airway obstruction. “Epidemiological Findings showed three of the five deceased children were zero-dose (unvaccinated). “The mother reported that two children had been immunised, but there was no evidence of Routine Immunization (RI) cards, as they were reportedly lost during relocation,”. The DG appealed to caregivers to visit the nearest primary healthcare facility for missed doses, report of unusual illnesses or visit the nearest LGA Disease Surveillance and Notification Officer (DSNO). He urged the public not to delay or rely on self-medication, adding that diphtheria is a severe, vaccine-preventable disease spread through respiratory droplets and close contact. “It can cause sore throat, fever, neck swelling, and difficulty breathing. Multiple child deaths in one household represent a serious public health signal. “The report of five child deaths in one household is a serious signal requiring continuous vigilance,” he said. The KNCDC boss urged all residents to prioritise routine immunisation, seek care early, and support public health response efforts in order to prevent diphtheria deaths and reduce outbreaks in Kano State. (NAN) The post Diphtheria: Kano disease control centre confirms 5 family members dead appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: PRP to Tinubu: Stop killings now; don’t wait till 2027
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The Peoples Redemption Party, PRP, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to stop the killings and abductions ravaging parts of the country, declaring that Nigerians cannot wait until 2027 for relief from worsening insecurity. The party accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) administration of failing in its primary duty to protect lives and property, alleging that the government was more interested in securing another term than addressing the dangers confronting ordinary Nigerians. In a statement by its National Chairman, Dr Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, the PRP said the growing impunity of criminal groups had left citizens at the mercy of attackers, while the government responded with press releases and platitudes. “The scale of the killings and abductions of helpless citizens and the rising impunity of their tormentors suggests that Nigerians live in a lawless country,” Baba-Ahmed said. He listed Kwara, Niger, Benue, Kebbi, Zamfara, Sokoto, Kaduna, Borno, Plateau and Yobe among states affected by the attacks, warning that Nigerians continued to lose their lives, livelihoods, property and freedom. The party also raised concerns over the pressure on military personnel and civilian volunteers battling insecurity, saying the crisis was threatening communities and the economic survival of millions. “Our gallant military and sundry volunteers are hard-pressed and virtually at the mercy of this expanding industry that feeds on lives, livelihood and economy of millions of our people,” Baba-Ahmed said. The PRP further accused the Tinubu administration of deploying huge sums of money to win the support of a small circle of Nigerians for what it described as a poisoned political ambition, even as citizens continued to bear the cost of insecurity. Urging Nigerians to speak out against the killings, Baba-Ahmed insisted that the president had a duty to protect citizens before the end of his tenure. “President Tinubu still has four months to go before his defeat. He has a responsibility to live up to his oath to protect lives and the welfare of Nigerians,” he said. The post PRP to Tinubu: Stop killings now; don’t wait till 2027 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le monde au-delà des États, une géopolitique des acteurs non étatiques
items.description: Les États souverains dominent nos représentations du monde. Pourtant, une part croissante des fonctions traditionnellement attachées à la souveraineté se déploie hors du seul cadre étatique. Multinationales, plateformes numériques, diasporas, organisations non gouvernementales (ONG), organisations sportives, groupes armés ou entités en quête de reconnaissance investissent des domaines que l’État leur concède, qui échappent à sa maîtrise ou dont le contrôle lui est disputé. Ces formes de pouvoir ne sont pas nouvelles, mais l’échelle de leurs moyens, leur transnationalité et leurs capacités à exercer des formes d’autorité modifient les rapports de force internationaux. À l'occasion de la parution de la Revue internationale et stratégique (RIS) N°143 sur le thème « Le monde au-delà des États, une géopolitique des acteurs non étatiques », Lukas Aubin, directeur de recherche à l’IRIS, responsable du Programme Sport et géopolitique et de l’Observatoire géopolitique de l’espace post-soviétique, et Fatou Élise Ba, chercheuse à l’IRIS, responsable du Programme Sécurité humaine répondent à nos questions : Pourquoi est-il devenu indispensable d'analyser les rapports de force entre acteurs non étatiques et puissances étatiques ? Comment ces pouvoirs alternatifs parviennent-ils à la fois à avoir une capacité d’influence ou de contraindre un État, tout en restant dépendant structurellement de celui-ci ? Où se situe la frontière juridique et politique entre un État de facto et un État de jure ? L’article Le monde au-delà des États, une géopolitique des acteurs non étatiques est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

items.title: Compétition du 22 au 25 octobre : « Ngor Marlin Cup » de retour à Dakar
items.description: La prestigieuse Ngor Marlin Cup fait son grand retour à Dakar, du 22 au 25 octobre 2026. Selon un communiqué de presse de la Fédération sénégalaise de pêche sportive (Fsps), cette édition s’annonce comme l’une des plus relevées du continent, avec la participation de plusieurs grandes nations de la discipline. Outre le Sénégal, présenté comme un sérieux prétendant au titre, l’Afrique du Sud, le Canada, la France et l’Italie ont confirmé leur présence. Au total, 25 bateaux prendront part à ces quatre journées de compétition, au départ de la baie de Ngor. Les équipes, composées de pêcheurs d’élite, rivaliseront de stratégie et d’endurance pour traquer le marlin bleu, l’une des espèces les plus convoitées de l’océan Atlantique. A lire aussi : 37e Traversée Dakar-Gorée : Ousseynou Diop règne, Aïcha Diop surprend Les pêcheurs évolueront au large de Dakar, notamment autour des dispositifs de concentration de poissons, réputés pour attirer thons et marlins bleus. Au-delà de la compétition, la Ngor Marlin Cup met en lumière le potentiel maritime du Sénégal et la position de Dakar comme destination prisée pour le tourisme de pêche et l’écotourisme. La manifestation met également l’accent sur la préservation des ressources halieutiques, à travers la pratique du « catch and release », consistant à marquer puis relâcher les poissons capturés. Les passionnés, les professionnels du secteur et les curieux sont invités à suivre les pesées quotidiennes, qui promettent des moments forts en émotion, et à célébrer l’esprit de la Teranga. Par ailleurs, sur le plan international, l’équipe nationale du Sénégal de pêche sportive se préparera également à un autre rendez-vous majeur : les Championnats du monde, prévus en Espagne. Fama NDIAYE

items.title: Human trafficking: NAPTIP, ICMPD, ECOWAS move to tighten airport surveillance
items.description: By Matthew Johnson The National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP), the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) and the International Centre for Migration Policy Development (ICMPD) have called for stronger collaboration among aviation stakeholders to prevent human trafficking through Nigerian airports. The call was made on Tuesday, October 13, 2026, at a three-day awareness and sensitisation workshop for aviation stakeholders in Lagos. The workshop aimed to strengthen the implementation of the Trafficking in Persons (Control of Activities of Organisations and Centres) Regulations, 2019, and improve inter-agency cooperation in the fight against human trafficking. Speaking at the workshop, NAPTIP’s Director of Intelligence in charge of Research and Programme Development, Mr Josiah Emerole, who represented the agency’s Director-General, Binta Bello, said many stakeholders operating at airports did not fully understand their responsibilities under existing anti-trafficking laws. Emerole said the workshop was organised to equip airport personnel, labour recruiters, civil society organisations and other migration-sector actors with the knowledge needed to identify suspected trafficking victims and report suspicious activities. He explained that traffickers often presented their victims as ordinary passengers with apparently valid travel documents, making it necessary for frontline personnel to look beyond documentation and examine the circumstances surrounding their journeys. According to him, officers should be alert to inconsistencies in passengers’ travel plans, financial circumstances, destinations and explanations for travelling, as these could indicate possible exploitation. He said, “It is not just about looking at the person’s documents. It is a question of talking to the person, using some psychological and emotional strategies for the person to tell the truth.” Emerole noted that some victims were unaware of the exploitation awaiting them at their destinations, adding that timely intervention by airport personnel could prevent them from falling into the hands of traffickers. He said that although traffickers continued to exploit international airports, increased surveillance and awareness had contributed to a reduction in the use of Nigerian airports by some criminal networks, forcing them to explore alternative routes through other countries. He, however, stressed the need for sustained training and stronger cooperation among agencies to close existing gaps. Emerole disclosed that NAPTIP would establish a working group involving relevant stakeholders to coordinate activities and monitor progress through reports from agencies operating at different airports and other relevant data. He said, “I will say immigration officers, aviation personnel, labour recruiters and other stakeholders should understand their responsibilities under the Trafficking in Persons (Prohibition), Enforcement and Administration Act, 2015, and the 2019 regulations.” Also speaking, the Project Manager at ICMPD, Mr Matthias Esene, said the organisation was supporting Nigeria and other West African countries in strengthening migration management and preventing trafficking while protecting the right to freedom of movement. Esene, who represented the head of the organisation’s Nigeria office, said the workshop was supported through regional migration initiatives, including the Free Movement of Persons and Migration project, organised by ICMPD in collaboration with NAPTIP and funded by the European Union and the Kingdom of Denmark. He explained that ICMPD worked with government institutions and civil society organisations to improve their capacity to respond to migration-related challenges and strengthen cooperation among agencies responsible for protecting migrants. According to him, the 2019 regulations provide a framework for identifying trafficking-related indicators, referring suspected victims to appropriate services and providing psychosocial support. He said the challenge was to ensure that stakeholders understood and implemented the provisions effectively, particularly those relating to their individual responsibilities and cooperation with other agencies. He added that frontline officials were responsible for identifying vulnerable persons and suspected trafficking victims without unnecessarily restricting the movement of legitimate travellers. “Freedom of movement remains a right under the ECOWAS Protocol. Efforts to prevent trafficking should not undermine legitimate migration. “Freedom of movement is a right. Human trafficking is not something we appreciate,” Esene said. In his remarks, the ECOWAS Commission’s expert on anti-trafficking in persons and migration, Mr Osandu Ekeh, said trafficking remained a significant challenge in Nigeria and across West Africa, with criminal networks increasingly exploiting legitimate transport systems and travel services. Ekeh, who delivered remarks on behalf of the Acting Director of Humanitarian and Social Affairs at the ECOWAS Commission, Dr Mohamed Ibrahim, said the aviation sector was strategically positioned to help prevent, detect and report trafficking-related activities. He said the commission had been coordinating regional anti-trafficking interventions through its regional action plan covering 2018 to 2027. Ekeh explained that ECOWAS, its member states and ICMPD had also worked on initiatives to strengthen prevention, particularly in protecting women, children and other vulnerable groups from trafficking and related crimes. He said the commission had supported assistance programmes for trafficking victims, including medical care, psychological support, reintegration and vocational training. Ekeh emphasised that effective implementation of the 2019 regulations required greater awareness and cooperation among immigration officers, aviation personnel, travel agencies, labour recruiters, maritime regulators and other frontline actors. He urged participants to move beyond awareness creation and develop practical mechanisms for sharing information, identifying suspected cases and supporting victims. Similarly, Bamidele Jomole called for strict enforcement of the regulations and closer cooperation among aviation authorities, immigration, customs, labour and justice officials, as well as civil society organisations. Jomole said the participation of controllers from the country’s three international airports was a significant development in efforts to strengthen the fight against trafficking. He urged relevant authorities to verify that licensed labour recruitment agencies had the appropriate NAPTIP clearances and ensure that recruitment and travel arrangements complied with existing regulations. “The workshop should produce concrete commitments and a communiqué that would guide participating institutions in identifying loopholes exploited by traffickers and coordinating measures to close them,” Jomole said. Earlier, an ICMPD representative, Ifeoluwa Sinkaiye, said the workshop was designed to strengthen stakeholders’ understanding of trafficking trends, risk indicators and their respective obligations under existing laws. Sinkaiye said participants would examine relevant legal frameworks, discuss emerging trafficking methods and undertake practical exercises to improve coordination in responding to suspected cases. She explained that the programme would also produce recommendations and a communiqué to guide future interventions, while an evaluation would assess participants’ knowledge and readiness to apply what they had learnt. Sinkaiye urged stakeholders to translate the knowledge gained into practical action in their daily duties, noting that effective collaboration among agencies was essential to preventing trafficking and protecting vulnerable persons. The workshop brought together representatives of relevant government agencies, airport operators, labour recruitment organisations and other stakeholders from Lagos, Abuja, Kano, Ghana and other locations. The post Human trafficking: NAPTIP, ICMPD, ECOWAS move to tighten airport surveillance appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2028 Olympic Games qualification ‘really tough’ – Black Queens coach Björkegren
items.description: Black Queens head coach Lars Kim Björkegren has described the path to qualifying for the 2028 Olympic Games as “really tough” but says he “believe[s] in the girls” to get the job done. Having received a bye in the first preliminary round of the qualifiers, the Queens dispatched Mauritius 10-0 to progress to the next phase. The senior women’s national team will face Zambia in the third round, scheduled for 23 February to 6 March 2027. A total of 16 nations will compete in the third round of the African qualifiers, with the continent having just two slots at the global showpiece. “We have the potential to go all the way,” Björkegren said. “In football, there is no easy game, especially when it comes to qualifying for the Olympics, as only two countries from Africa will go to Los Angeles. “It is really tough and to get there, we need to win. I believe in the girls and I think we [will] be there.” The Black Queens have never qualified for the Olympic Games in the country’s history.

items.title: Police culturelle : les talents artistiques des forces de sécurité à l’honneur
items.description: La première édition de la « Police culturelle » s'est tenue le samedi 10 octobre 2026, au Musée des civilisations noires. Cet événement, à l'initiative de l'Association de la presse culturelle du Sénégal (Apcs) et de la Police nationale, a permis de mettre à l'honneur les talents artistiques et littéraires des forces de sécurité à travers une diversité d'expressions artistiques. Le Musée des civilisations noires a accueilli, le samedi 10 octobre, la première édition de la « Police culturelle ». Cette manifestation, portée par l'Association de la presse culturelle du Sénégal (Apcs), en collaboration avec la Direction générale de la Police nationale, a mis en lumière les talents artistiques et littéraires des membres des forces de sécurité. Ce qui a notamment retenu l'attention du représentant du ministre de la Communication et des Relations avec les institutions. Moustapha Thioune a exprimé son émerveillement face à la diversité des talents présentés, allant de la peinture à la musique, en passant par la littérature. A lire aussi : La Police nationale mise sur l’espagnol pour renforcer ses compétences De son côté, le président de l'Apcs a insisté sur la nécessité de promouvoir la paix et le civisme. « Mon ambition est de promouvoir une culture de paix, de civisme, de responsabilité et de respect mutuel à travers des initiatives concrètes. Nous devons encourager les initiatives qui rapprochent la Police nationale de la population, particulièrement de la jeunesse », a déclaré Alioune Badara Mané. Le directeur général de la Police nationale, Mame Seydou Ndour, a rappelé les ambitions de cette première édition de la « Police culturelle ». « Nous voulons une police proche de ses concitoyens, nous voulons une police qui dialogue autant qu'elle protège, nous voulons une police qui reconnaît et encourage les talents dans ses rangs. Nous voulons faire de la culture un levier de paix, de cohésion sociale et de citoyenneté », a-t-il déclaré. Mame Seydou Ndour a également profité de l'occasion pour rendre un vibrant hommage à une figure marquante de la police et de la culture : Laye Bamba Seck, ancien policier et homme de culture. « Avant nous, il avait compris qu'on peut servir la nation sous l'uniforme tout en donnant sa voix, sa plume et son talent à la culture, sans jamais trahir ni l'un ni l'autre. Laye Bamba Seck est le symbole de ce que nous voulons rappeler : la culture a toujours eu sa place dans la maison police », a-t-il souligné. La manifestation s'est achevée par des démonstrations de rap et de slam, des performances de lutteurs ainsi que des présentations d'arts martiaux par les agents. Fatou NGOM (Stagiaire)

items.title: GRFU, GOC Women’s Commission hold breast cancer awareness, expresses gratitude to Sunda International Ghana
items.description: The Ghana Rugby Football Union (GRFU), in collaboration with the Women’s Commission of the Ghana Olympic Committee (GOC), has held a breast cancer awareness education programme for female athletes, coaches, officials and community members. The initiative focused on the importance of early detection, regular self-examination and screening in the prevention and management of breast cancer. The organisers said the programme was aimed at improving awareness among women involved in sports and encouraging them to take early action when they notice potential symptoms. President of the Ghana Rugby Football Union expressed appreciation to Sunda International Ghana Ltd, makers of Softcare, for supporting the initiative. “Breast cancer affects all women, including our athletes,” the President said. The President said the partnership had helped educate and encourage participants to pay greater attention to their health. The GRFU and the GOC Women’s Commission said they remained committed to promoting women’s health, safety and well-being through sports. They also thanked Sunda International Ghana for its support towards the breast cancer awareness activities. Credit: Ghana Rugby Football Union
